news.titleEn: Former Fed Adviser’s Prison Sentence Puts Insider Misappropriation Risks Back in Focus
news.titleZh: 前美联储顾问被判刑，内幕信息滥用风险再受关注
news.summaryZh: 美国司法部对一名前美联储理事会顾问判处联邦监禁，此案警示内幕交易风险不仅限于上市公司高管、银行家或对冲基金，也涉及政府及准政府内部人员滥用通过信任职位获取的市场敏感信息。该案强化了现代内幕交易执法中的核心原则：检察官会积极运用盗用理论追诉将非公开信息用于个人利益的行为，即使信息来源是联邦机构。对于诉讼律师，此案是界定信义义务和保密义务的标志；对于内部法律顾问和合规团队，教训更为广泛：许多机构雇佣前监管人员、央行职员等，合规计划应重新审查入职问卷、限制名单控制、跨墙程序等，培训应涉及宏观经济、政策和监管信息的滥用。该判决也凸显了白领执法与金融监管的融合，公司应评估监控系统是否能够检测与政策事件相关的交易模式。司法部继续强调个人责任，内部调查必须迅速，文件保存应尽早开始，单个员工滥用机密政府信息可能造成重大后果。
news.bodyHtml:
The Justice Department’s sentencing of a former adviser to the Federal Reserve Board of Governors is one of the clearest recent reminders that insider-trading exposure is not limited to public-company executives, bankers, or hedge funds. It also reaches government and quasi-government insiders who misuse market-sensitive information obtained through positions of trust.

According to the government’s announcement, the former Fed adviser received a federal prison sentence after being prosecuted for exploiting confidential economic information. The case is legally significant because it reinforces a core principle in modern insider-trading enforcement: prosecutors will pursue misappropriation theories aggressively where a defendant allegedly converts nonpublic information for personal gain, even when the source is a federal institution rather than a traditional corporate issuer.

For litigators, the matter is a useful marker of how criminal authorities continue to frame fiduciary-duty and confidentiality breaches in market cases. Expect this sentencing to be cited in future disputes over materiality, duty, and the scope of protected government information. Defense counsel in parallel civil or regulatory matters should also note the reputational impact of these prosecutions; once the government characterizes conduct as abuse of public trust, settlement dynamics can shift quickly.

For in-house counsel and compliance teams, the lesson is broader than insider trading in the classic sense. Many institutions employ former regulators, central-bank staff, policy advisers, and consultants who may have had access to sensitive information in prior roles. Compliance programs should revisit onboarding questionnaires, restricted-list controls, wall-crossing procedures, personal trading certifications, and escalation protocols for employees with government backgrounds. Training should also address misuse of macroeconomic, policy, and supervisory information—not just issuer-specific earnings or M&A intelligence.

The development also underscores the convergence of white-collar enforcement and financial regulation. Prosecutors increasingly view the integrity of markets as tied to the integrity of government processes. That means companies operating near regulated markets—broker-dealers, asset managers, fintechs, and public issuers—should assess whether their surveillance systems are calibrated to detect trading patterns connected to policy events, rate-sensitive announcements, or confidential regulatory actions.

More broadly, the sentence fits an enforcement environment in which DOJ continues to emphasize individual accountability. For legal professionals, that has practical implications: internal investigations must move quickly, document preservation should begin early, and decisions about employee discipline, disclosures, and cooperation need to be made with criminal exposure in mind. Even absent a sprawling corporate case, a single employee’s misuse of confidential government information can create significant investigative, civil, and reputational fallout.

news.titleEn: New Associate Hiring is Flat – Is AI The Cause?
news.titleZh: 新律师招聘停滞不前——人工智能是原因吗？
news.summaryZh:
美国法律市场整体增长，但AmLaw 200律所的新律师招聘数量在过去四年保持平稳甚至略有下降。2021年因疫情后招聘激增成为异常值，而同期律所收入增长数千亿美元。与此同时，有经验的横向律师招聘数量在2025年已超过新律师。

人工智能可能对招聘数据产生影响，但程度尚不明确。2025年许多律所已大规模使用AI工具，客户也利用AI处理常规任务，减少了对初级律师的需求。然而，新律师招聘停滞趋势在AI广泛应用前就已出现，其他因素如律所对效率的追求、业务结构变化等也可能发挥作用。未来，AI与这些趋势结合可能进一步强化横向律师优于新律师的招聘格局。
news.bodyText: New data shows that entry-level associate hiring in the US has been flat for four years – despite overall legal market growth. Is this the impact of AI, or something else? Data from SurePoint’s Law School Hiring Report 2026 found that in the four previous years the number of new associates hired into AmLaw 200 firms, i.e. entry-level joiners from law school, went as follows: I.e. generally flat, with a small decline overall, at a time when the AmLaw 200 have seen tremendous growth and a very busy few years. Note that 2021 was an outlier caused by a sudden surge in hiring following Covid in 2020. It’s estimated that during those four years the AmLaw 200 added several tens of billions of dollars in combined revenues, yet as seen above, the number of newbies in the US stayed flat, or dropped. That seems counter-intuitive, as a growing market would normally demand more entry-level attorneys to ‘feed the engine’. Meanwhile, the number of lateral associate hires, i.e. more experienced lawyers who are hired from other law firms, rose over the last three years after an initial surge and a short drop after Covid. In fact, last year in 2025, there were more laterals than newbies. Is That You AI? So, is this the impact of AI? In previous years this site would have said ‘no’. Why? Because legal AI uptake was just not broad enough, or its use meaningful enough, to have much of an impact. Yet, many firms by 2025 probably were using AI tools at scale, and in 2026 many more will be. At the same time, many clients are also using AI for routine tasks – some of which would have been sent out to the junior lawyers at AmLaw 200 firms. So, potentially a double impact. Therefore, it seems reasonable now to suggest that AI is playing into these figures. The challenge is we don’t know how much yet, or where this is heading. There is however, another challenge. The trend toward flat newbie hiring started before widescale legal AI use. So, what else is happening? AL’s guess would be that regardless of AI, some of the below factors may be in play: Overall, AL would estimate that these potential trends, added to greater AI use, will combine further in the years to come to create even more powerful conditions that favour laterals over newbies. The data also underlines – AL would argue – the need for law firms to train up junior lawyers more rapidly, so they can deliver more valuable work product, especially as AI chews up the entry-level tasks.

news.titleEn: Clifford Chance Launches AI KM Platform With Microsoft + Epiq
news.titleZh: 高伟绅律师事务所携手微软与Epiq推出AI知识管理平台
news.summaryZh: 高伟绅律师事务所（Clifford Chance）推出了一款AI赋能的知识管理平台，该平台由微软（Microsoft）和Epiq Advisory合作开发。平台名为Knowledge Bank，已收录超过40万份文档，旨在将律所数十年的专业知识整合到一个安全、AI就绪的存储库中。平台基于Microsoft 365、Power Platform、Azure和Azure AI Studio构建，能够根据律师的工作、角色、地点和具体需求提供上下文相关的知识。该平台是律所向客户提供价值战略的核心，与Epiq和微软的合作使得在尊重客户保密性的前提下部署AI成为可能。该平台重新定义了法律知识的策展、治理和AI激活方式，并嵌入律师工作流程。高伟绅与微软的长期合作关系根植于创新和为客户创造有意义的影响。
news.bodyText: Clifford Chance has launched an AI-enabled KM platform, developed in partnership with Microsoft and Epiq Advisory. It continues a deep relationship with the tech giant. The platform already contains more than 400,000 documents, they said. The new Knowledge Bank ‘curates decades of the firm’s expertise within a secure, AI-ready repository’. It was built using Microsoft 365, Power Platform, Azure, and Azure AI Studio. The platform delivers ‘knowledge in context – aligned to a lawyer’s work, role, location, and specific requirements – while drawing from a broader set of sources and formats’, they added. Some of its key aspects include: Matt Taylor, Partner, Global Head of Knowledge & Training at Clifford Chance, commented: ‘The creation of our new Knowledge Bank is central to our strategy of delivering value to our clients. Our work with Epiq Advisory for Law Firms and Microsoft allows us to curate decades of firm knowledge in a repository that enables the deployment of AI while respecting client confidentiality. ‘Clients will benefit from efficiencies and insights made possible by AI and other new technologies, underpinned by our specialist expertise and not just off-the-shelf solutions.’ Kieron Champion, Managing Director & Advisory Practice Lead, Epiq Advisory for Law Firms, added: ‘Partnering with Clifford Chance and Microsoft, we have helped build a Microsoft-native platform that redefines how legal knowledge can be curated, governed, and activated through AI – embedded directly in the lawyer workflow. Moreover, this solution creates a foundation that liberates Clifford Chance to innovate on its own terms.’ And Paul Barlow, Technology Strategist – Legal Services, Microsoft, concluded: ‘Clifford Chance and Microsoft have a long-standing relationship rooted in a shared focus on innovation and delivering technologies that create meaningful impact for the firm and its clients. ‘From being one of the first global law firms to deploy Microsoft 365 Copilot, to now exploring the use of AI to reimagine how the firm harnesses its valuable knowledge assets, the firm’s work with Epiq Advisory for Law Firms reflects Clifford Chance’s commitment to leveraging advanced technologies to deliver client value and enhance lawyer productivity.’ Is this a big deal? Well, it’s a sign of how much Microsoft wants to do more than just provide basic infrastructure to the legal sector – and clearly this project needed a lot of customisation and engineering, which Epiq provided a big part of. Major KM and DMS players will no doubt be watching this very closely…!

news.titleEn: The week the war reached Russia’s e-commerce supply chain
news.titleZh: 战争蔓延至俄罗斯电商供应链的一周
news.summaryZh: 7月15日至18日，乌克兰无人机袭击了俄罗斯电商Wildberries位于莫斯科东部埃列克特罗斯塔利和坦波夫地区科托夫斯克的物流中心，造成9人死亡、80多人受伤。乌克兰总统泽连斯基称这些设施被用于供应制裁组件以生产无人机和导航设备，但该说法未获独立证实。Wildberries创始人表示公司可能损失10%至15%的仓库空间。同期，乌克兰还袭击了黑海和亚速海的172艘俄罗斯船只，包括影子舰队油轮。海上行动正将俄精锐无人机部队从前线调离，同时挤压能源和农业物流。对贸易合规、供应链尽职调查及证据核实专业人士而言，这一周展示了现代战争如何通过物流网络、炼油能力、航运通道和信息系统展开。
news.bodyHtml:
Editor’s Note: Warehouses that fill Russia’s online shopping orders burned this week, and those fires say as much about the direction of the war as any map of the front. Between July 15 and July 18, Ukrainian strikes reached e-commerce logistics hubs, shadow fleet tankers, refineries and, by Kyiv’s account, a strategic bomber, while Moscow’s stock exchange posted its steepest one-day drop since 2022 and President Vladimir Putin’s approval slid by 5 points in a week.

For cybersecurity, data privacy, regulatory compliance and eDiscovery professionals, the week reads as a working brief. Sanctioned components allegedly moving through consumer logistics networks, Indian gasoline reaching Russia through a ship-to-ship transfer, and satellite data independently testing official statements all touch the disciplines of trade screening, supply chain diligence and evidence verification.

Watch three threads from here: whether Ukraine sustains its maritime and refinery campaign, whether Kyiv’s reshuffled cabinet steadies after rare wartime protests, and whether hybrid pressure on NATO’s eastern flank escalates beyond surveillance flights.

Industry News – Geopolitics Beat

The week the war reached Russia’s e-commerce supply chain

ComplexDiscovery Staff

The fires that lit the sky over Elektrostal, east of Moscow, and Kotovsk, in Russia’s Tambov region, overnight from July 17 into July 18 did not start at military bases. They started in fulfillment centers serving Russian shoppers.

By morning, Russian officials counted nine dead and over 80 wounded across the overnight attack series, according to The Associated Press, with most of the casualties at facilities of Wildberries, the country’s largest online retailer.

The strikes on two Wildberries logistics hubs closed a four-day stretch, July 15 through July 18, in which the war between Russia and Ukraine looked less like a contest of trenches and increasingly like a contest of systems: logistics networks, refining capacity, shipping lanes, equity markets, and the information channels through which both governments claim success. For professionals who track sanctions exposure, supply chain risk, and information integrity, the week offered a compressed case study in how a modern war is now fought and measured.

Commerce becomes a target set

Ukrainian drones struck the two Wildberries warehouses in waves through the night. Seven warehouse workers died in Kotovsk and 25 were wounded there, according to Russian regional officials cited by CBS News. Moscow Region Governor Andrei Vorobyov said 37 people were wounded in his region, one of whom later died in a hospital. CNN described the attacks as among the deadliest Ukrainian strikes inside Russia in two years.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy characterized the facilities as part of a sanctioned-component supply chain. “These facilities were used by the aggressor to supply sanctioned components for the production of drones and navigation equipment,” he said in remarks reported by CBS News.

The claim, which has not been independently verified, reframes an e-commerce fulfillment network as a sanctions-evasion artery. Meduza reported that Wildberries may have lost the use of 10 to 15 percent of its warehouse space, citing The Bell; the company has published no damage assessment of its own. Wildberries founder Tatyana Kim called it “a terrible night, terrible events for our company and for our country” and pledged support for victims’ families, Novaya Gazeta Europe reported. Two points deserve separation here. Trade compliance teams should take the practical one: screening obligations do not stop at the freight forwarder, and dual-use components can travel through consumer logistics channels that rarely appear on traditional risk maps. The legal one is narrower: even if sanctioned components moved through a fulfillment center, that alone would not settle whether the facility was a lawful military objective, a question the law of armed conflict answers through a separate test of effective contribution to military action and definite military advantage, and one no public evidence yet permits outsiders to assess. Russia’s defense ministry, for its part, said its air defenses intercepted 379 Ukrainian drones across 19 regions and occupied Crimea overnight, a figure that could not be independently confirmed.

Tankers, refineries and a bomber Russia no longer builds

The warehouse strikes extended a campaign that spent the week working through Russia’s energy and maritime logistics. Unmanned Systems Forces Commander Robert “Madyar” Brovdi said on July 18 that Ukrainian drones struck 172 Russian vessels in the Black Sea and Sea of Azov between July 6 and July 18, a tally that includes tankers linked to Russia’s sanctions-evading shadow fleet and that has not been independently verified. Analysts at the Institute for the Study of War (ISW) assessed that the maritime campaign is pulling elite Russian drone units away from the front line and squeezing energy and agricultural logistics at the same time.

Refineries burned too. Ukrainian strikes hit the Slavneft-YANOS refinery complex in Yaroslavl during the week, and the cumulative damage to Russian refining capacity has begun producing a result few would have predicted three years ago: Russia is importing gasoline from India. Reuters reported that the tanker Agni departed India’s Vadinar Port with 42,000 metric tons of gasoline in mid-June, transferred the cargo at sea to a second tanker, the Garnet, near Egypt in early July, and that the Garnet is expected at Vitino Port in Murmansk around July 26. Sanctions investigators scrutinize such ship-to-ship transfers because they can complicate cargo tracing.

The most symbolically loaded strike of the week came at Engels-2 air base in Saratov Oblast, roughly 800 kilometers from the Ukrainian border. Ukraine’s Security Service said it critically damaged a Tu-95MS strategic bomber there, releasing footage it said showed the aircraft’s tail section severed. The claimed loss had not been independently confirmed, and Russian authorities did not acknowledge it. The Tu-95 is an airframe the Soviet Union stopped producing decades ago and Russia no longer builds. “We are increasing the price Russia pays for its aggression against our country and our people,” Zelenskyy said in remarks reported by the Kyiv Independent.

The systems war ran in both directions. Russian missile and drone strikes during the window kept working through Ukrainian energy facilities and Black Sea port infrastructure, part of a campaign that, Reuters reported, citing industry sources and a Ukrainian Agri Council report, had eliminated about one-third of Ukraine’s Black Sea grain-export capacity. The July 15 assessment recorded Russia resuming strikes against Ukrainian port infrastructure with the assessed aim of degrading the economy and export capacity, and overnight packages through the week ran to 146 drones and multiple ballistic and cruise missiles in a single night. Ukraine’s warehouses, substations and ports have absorbed this pressure for years; what changed this week is how much of it Russia absorbed in return.

Moscow’s markets and pollsters flash warnings

Numbers inside Russia told their own story. The Moscow Exchange composite index fell 4.24 percent on July 16, its steepest single-day drop since September 2022. Gazprom shares touched 83.98 rubles the same day, an all-time low that undercut a record standing since October 2008, after The Wall Street Journal reported that talks with China over the Power of Siberia 2 pipeline had stalled on price. VTB Bank shares also hit a record low.

Polling released that week pointed to a separate source of domestic strain. Russia’s state-affiliated Public Opinion Foundation recorded a 5 percentage point drop in President Vladimir Putin’s approval rating in its July 10 to 12 survey, to about 66 percent, which Meduza characterized as the steepest weekly decline since the full-scale invasion began. The state-run pollster VTsIOM measured approval at 65.1 percent. Fuel shortages, internet restrictions and a blocked Telegram figured among the causes cited. Bloomberg reported that wealthy Russians, including associates of Putin, have been shifting assets toward cryptocurrency, gold and foreign property amid concerns about Kremlin nationalization.

None of this means the Russian state is buckling. It does mean the financial data trail, from tanker transponders to exchange indices to satellite imagery, now offers outside analysts a near-real-time read on strain that the Kremlin cannot fully script.

Kyiv reshuffles its government under fire

Ukraine spent the same week absorbing a political storm of its own. Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov, a popular figure credited with building Ukraine’s drone and technology programs, lost his post in a government reshuffle initiated by President Zelenskyy, triggering protests in Kyiv and cities across the country, a rare wartime display of public dissent. Parliament confirmed Serhii Koretskyi, who had led the state energy company Naftogaz since 2025, as prime minister on July 16 with 289 votes, replacing Yulia Svyrydenko.

David Arakhamia, who heads Zelenskyy’s parliamentary faction, said Koretskyi’s energy experience “will be invaluable, especially now as Ukraine prepares for what could be the most difficult winter in its history,” according to Euronews.

The fallout and the reshuffle moved on separate tracks. Serhiy Beskrestnov, a prominent drone and electronic warfare adviser, announced after Fedorov’s dismissal that he would no longer assist the defense ministry. Vitalii Kim, by contrast, left the Mykolaiv governorship because parliament appointed him veterans affairs minister in the new cabinet. Wartime governance, the week demonstrated, is itself contested terrain, and personnel files can move markets and morale as surely as artillery.

A front line measured in motorcycles

The ground war, by contrast, barely moved. ISW recorded no confirmed advances by either side on July 17 or July 18 across the major axes in Donetsk, Kharkiv and Zaporizhia oblasts, a finding about available evidence rather than proof that no movement occurred. Russia’s defense ministry is prioritizing motorcycles, buggies and all-terrain vehicles over armored mechanized systems, a procurement pattern ISW read as a commitment to slow, grinding positional warfare. A Ukrainian officer in the Slovyansk direction said Russian assaults have climbed from five to seven per day in the spring to as many as 26 daily, with Russian forces relying on small infiltration groups rather than mechanized columns.

Claims outran evidence on both sides of the information front. Russian Chief of the General Staff Valery Gerasimov announced advances in Donetsk Oblast that ISW found uncorroborated by available visual evidence. The discipline that catches such gaps, matching official statements against geolocated footage and satellite data, is the same discipline eDiscovery and investigations professionals apply to any contested record. Meduza, citing NASA VIIRS Black Marble satellite data, reported that nighttime illumination across occupied Crimea had fallen to roughly one-fifth of normal levels at the end of June and had not recovered, a data-driven check on official reassurances about conditions on the peninsula.

Beyond Ukraine, Polish and Swedish fighters intercepted two Russian Su-30SM2 jets over the Baltic Sea during NATO air defense exercises, a day after allied jets intercepted a Russian Il-20 reconnaissance plane; neither incident was reported as an airspace violation. “Russia is testing the alliance’s readiness in this way,” Polish Deputy Prime Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz said. Warsaw and Baltic governments have said Russia may stage a false flag operation against NATO territory, and Ukrainska Pravda reported earlier this month that Washington warned Poland that Moscow may test the alliance with a hybrid attack, an operation that could involve cyber, sabotage or information activity before, or instead of, any conventional attack. The week’s daily assessments recorded no negotiation developments.

What the week’s ledger says

Add the four days up and the pattern is hard to miss. The war’s center of gravity kept shifting away from the trench line and toward the systems that sustain it: warehouses, tankers, refineries, stock exchanges, polling desks and cabinet rooms. Professionals responsible for sanctions compliance should track the India-to-Russia fuel route and the components moving through consumer logistics networks. Those responsible for information integrity should note how satellite data and geolocated footage repeatedly tested official claims from both capitals, and how often the officials came up short.

The fires will be extinguished, and Wildberries can reroute orders through other facilities while it rebuilds. The harder question lingers past the smoke: when a war is waged against the systems that deliver daily life, from gasoline to groceries to next-day packages, how should the professionals who safeguard those systems, in any country, decide what counts as critical infrastructure worth protecting first?

news.bodyText:
According to recent studies, law firms have an AI problem on both sides of the business.

Not only are they slow to use AI and automation to serve clients as demonstrated by a recent Deloitte Legal study, but according to a new BigHand study, they’re also failing to use it to run their practices. Poor management of support staff and workflow not only impacts the lawyers and legal professionals, it also directly impacts client service and satisfaction. Clients that are more and more demanding better and cheaper results.

If firms want to keep business, they need to figure out how to use AI and automation acroass the board.

Here are my thoughts for Above the Law

news.summaryZh:
播客追求大受众群体的旧模式正在消退，对律所而言，这从来不是正确方向。今年欧洲最大播客会议的趋势显示，成功者不再追逐最大听众群，而是与特定群体建立真实关系并转化为业务。律所播客应被视为权威资产，而非媒体公司。

律所应将播客作为建立潜在客户信任的工具，而非追求广告收入或下载量。衡量标准应从下载量转向带来的客户数。每期节目应被多次利用，而非一次性发布。聚焦特定客户群体的播客优于泛法律话题节目，因为精准受众更易信任并聘用律所。例如，为特许经营业主或医生定制的播客能成为资源，吸引真正需要帮助的客户。
news.bodyHtml:
A big audience used to be the whole goal. Push the downloads up, land a sponsor, call it a win. That playbook is fading fast, and for law firms it was never the right one to begin with.

I just went through the takeaways from this year’s biggest podcasting conference in Europe, shared by the team at Riverside, the platform we use to record Counsel Cast. The shift was loud and clear. The people winning with podcasts right now are not the ones chasing the largest possible crowd. They are the ones building a real relationship with a specific group of people and turning that into business.

That lines up almost word for word with what Alex Sanfilippo told me on Counsel Cast. Your firm’s podcast is not a media company. It is an authority asset. Here is what is changing, and what it means for how you run your show.

Is a law firm podcast a media play or a business play?

It is a business play. The firms seeing real results treat their podcast as a way to build trust with future clients, not as a channel for ad revenue or download milestones.

The old energy was all about sponsorships and audience size. The new energy is about owned audiences and relationships that lead somewhere. For a creator, that might mean a paid community or a course. For a law firm, it means something more direct. Consultations. Retainers. Referrals. A prospect who has listened to ten of your episodes does not need to be convinced you know your stuff. They already trust you. They just need to know you are taking new clients.

When you stop measuring your show by downloads and start measuring it by the clients it brings in, every decision about the podcast gets easier.

Your episode is the start, not the finish

The biggest mistake I see firms make is treating each episode as a one-and-done. Record, publish, move on. That leaves most of the value on the table.

The smarter approach treats the episode as the engine for everything else. One recording can fuel a full month of content if you let it.

  • A blog post that goes deeper on one idea from the episode
  • A newsletter that pulls out the single most useful takeaway
  • Three to five short clips for social
  • A resource page on your website that builds your authority on a topic
  • Quote graphics and a carousel

You did the hard part when you recorded. Now get ten uses out of it instead of one.

Why niche beats reach for law firms

A focused show aimed at one type of client outperforms a broad legal topics show, because a specific audience trusts you faster and is far more likely to hire you.

For years the worry was that niching down too far would shrink your audience to nothing. The data now says the opposite. Smaller, focused shows are outperforming massive general ones when it comes to actual return, because the audience is the right audience.

Think about what this means for a firm. A podcast about legal issues is a crowded, forgettable space. A podcast for franchise owners navigating their first lawsuit, or for physicians dealing with licensing board complaints, is a resource. The people who need it will find it, stay, and call you. You are not trying to reach everyone. You are trying to reach the few hundred people who could become clients.

What your clients actually think about AI in podcasting

Listeners are comfortable with AI working behind the scenes, like transcripts, research, and show notes. They push back hard when AI touches the actual show, and a synthetic host voice is the single most disliked use of all.

This is good news for lawyers who feel torn about AI. New listener research shows people do not mind it doing the invisible work. Prep, transcription, brainstorming, cover art. That frees you up.

But the line is clear. The closer AI gets to the voice and the relationship, the more your audience resents it. For a law firm, where the entire point is trust, that line matters even more. Use AI to handle the busywork around your show. Keep your real voice on the mic.

Talk to one client, not a crowd

One idea from the conference stuck with me. A legendary broadcaster said he records as if he is speaking to one person he loves. Another talks close to the microphone on purpose, so it feels like a friend with an arm around your shoulder.

Your listener is almost always alone. In the car. On a walk. In the kitchen. They chose your voice for that moment.

Lawyers tend to default to the lecture. The courtroom voice. The voice that performs authority instead of building connection. Drop it. Picture one client, the kind you want more of, and talk to them. That single shift will do more for your show than any equipment upgrade.

One clear next step beats a list of options

This is where Alex was blunt, and he was right. The best podcasts have a singular call to action. One thing you want the listener to do.

Firms love to stack their asks. Subscribe, follow, book a call, download the guide, share with a friend. The listener hears all of it and does none of it. Pick the one action that matters most for this episode and ask for that. Then watch whether people actually take it, because that, not your download count, is how you know the show is working.

The takeaway

Law firm podcasting is growing up. The metrics that used to matter are giving way to the ones that always should have. Here is the short version:

  • Treat your podcast as an authority asset, not a media property
  • Get ten pieces of content out of every recording
  • Niche down on purpose, because focus is what converts
  • Let AI handle the work behind the scenes and keep your real voice front and center
  • Speak to one client, not a crowd
  • Ask for one clear next step and measure whether people take it

Alex Sanfilippo unpacks all of this in our full conversation, including how to land strong guests and how to keep your show consistent enough to compound.

Listen to the episode here: https://conroycreativecounsel.com/podcast-cat/episode-books/can-your-law-firms-podcast-become-a-go-to-legal-resource-with-alex-sanfilippo/

And if building authority and visibility is the goal for your firm, that is exactly what we do with the Authority Tour. Learn more at https://conroycreativecounsel.com/authority-tour/

A podcast about legal issues is a crowded, forgettable space. A podcast for franchise owners navigating their first lawsuit, or for physicians dealing with licensing board complaints, is a resource. The people who need it will find it, stay, and call you. You are not trying to reach everyone. You are trying to reach the few hundred people who could become clients.

news.titleEn: AI Glasses Not a Good Look in New York Courthouses
news.titleZh: 纽约州法院禁止佩戴AI眼镜进入法庭
news.summaryZh: 纽约州成为首个在全州法院系统禁止AI智能眼镜及其他具备录音录像功能的眼镜或头戴设备的州。该禁令自2026年7月20日起生效，适用于全州超过1200个法院设施，包括州、县、市、镇和村级法院。所有进入法院的人员，包括诉讼当事人、律师、证人、家属及法院工作人员，均不得携带此类设备。AI智能眼镜能够隐蔽地录制庭审过程、对话及参与者影像，对司法程序完整性、保密通信及法院安全构成威胁。佩戴处方智能眼镜者需携带传统眼镜进入法院。纽约州是首个实施此类全州禁令的州，但其他司法管辖区已通过地方法规或法院命令开始限制智能眼镜的使用。
news.bodyText: Find Your Next Job ! New York has become the first state to prohibit AI-enabled smart glasses and other recording-enabled eyewear in all state courthouses. The new policy reflects growing concern over the ability of these devices to discreetly capture audio, video, photographs, and AI-generated transcripts. Below are answers to some common questions about the new rule and what it may signal for how organizations approach this technology. Are AI Glasses Permitted in New York Courts? Effective July 20, 2026, according to a memorandum by New York’s Office of Court Administration Executive Director, Justin Barry, on July 1, 2026, the New York State Unified Court System prohibits visitors from bringing smart glasses and other eyewear or headwear equipped with cameras, microphones, or other recording technology into any New York state courthouse. The prohibition applies to more than 1,200 state, county, city, town, and village courts throughout the state. “This prohibition applies to all individuals entering court facilities, including litigants,attorneys, witnesses, family members, UCS employees, and all other individuals who seek to enter a UCS facility for any reason.” Why did New York adopt this policy? The court system explained that AI-enabled smart glasses present unique challenges because they can record proceedings, conversations, and participants without being readily apparent to others. The statewide rule is intended to reinforce existing prohibitions on unauthorized recording in court facilities and to protect the integrity of judicial proceedings, confidential communications, and courthouse security. Are prescription smart glasses prohibited? Yes. Individuals who wear prescription smart glasses are expected to bring a conventional pair of prescription glasses if they need to enter a courthouse. Is New York the first state to take this step? New York appears to be the first state to implement a statewide prohibition applicable to every state court. However, courts in other jurisdictions have already begun restricting smart glasses through local rules, courthouse policies, or individual judicial orders. As adoption of AI-enabled wearables accelerates, additional statewide restrictions would not be surprising.

news.titleEn: Five Reasons for NJ Employers to Adopt an Employee AI Acceptable Use Policy
news.titleZh: 新泽西州雇主采用员工人工智能可接受使用政策的五大理由
news.summaryZh:
人工智能工具在工作场所带来诸多潜在益处，但若管理不当，也可能引发重大法律、隐私和网络安全风险。采用员工人工智能可接受使用政策有助于管理这些风险。以下是人力资源专业人士和内部法律顾问应优先制定该政策的五大关键理由。

员工使用未经授权的公开AI工具处理工作任务，可能导致公司信息泄露，造成隐私、网络安全和合规风险。政策应明确批准经组织审查的AI工具，禁止使用未经授权的AI应用。员工使用AI工具可能产生法律和合规风险，如上传受版权保护材料、泄露个人信息、依赖不准确或有偏见的AI输出等。政策需明确允许和禁止的使用方式，规定可输入AI系统的信息类别，并要求对AI输出进行人工审核。AI工具与组织系统交互可能引入数据泄露、安全漏洞等风险，政策应建立治理标准，确保评估、批准和安全使用。员工使用AI工具应遵守现有行为准则和保密义务，政策应禁止生成深度伪造、冒充他人、制造歧视性内容等行为，以降低法律和声誉风险。
news.bodyText: Find Your Next Job ! AI tools offer a multitude of potential benefits in the workplace. They can also create significant legal, privacy, and cybersecurity risk if not properly managed. Adopting an employee AI Acceptable Use Policy can help manage that risk. Below are five key reasons why HR professionals and in-house counsel should prioritize the development of an AI Acceptable Use Policy. One of the most significant risks accompanying workplace AI adoption is the use of unauthorized, publicly available AI tools by employees to perform work-related tasks. When employees input company information into unapproved AI platforms, organizations may inadvertently expose confidential, proprietary, personal, or regulated data to third parties, creating significant privacy, cybersecurity, and compliance risks. To mitigate these risks, a clear AI Acceptable Use Policy will identify approved, organization-vetted AI tools and expressly prohibit the use of unauthorized AI applications for business purposes. Requiring employees to use only approved platforms helps ensure that AI solutions undergo appropriate review by legal, information security, privacy, compliance, and IT stakeholders before deployment. Employees’ use of AI tools can create a range of legal and compliance risks if not properly governed. For example, employees may inadvertently upload copyrighted materials, disclose employee personal information or confidential business data, record or monitor individuals without appropriate notice or consent, or rely on AI-generated output that is inaccurate, biased, or discriminatory. These activities can expose employers to potential liability under privacy, intellectual property, employment, and anti-discrimination laws, as well as sector-specific regulatory requirements. To mitigate these risks, a comprehensive AI Acceptable Use Policy will clearly define both permitted and prohibited uses of AI tools. It will also establish categories of information that may or may not be entered into AI systems, set parameters for the appropriate use of AI-generated content, and require human review of AI outputs before they are relied upon for business decisions. Employers should also consider incorporating requirements for use case risk assessments, approval processes, and ongoing monitoring to help ensure that AI tools are used responsibly, consistently, and in compliance with applicable legal and regulatory obligations. AI tools can interact with an organization’s systems, business processes, and data assets including, in some cases, confidential, proprietary, or personal information. As with any new technology, the use of an AI tool can introduce additional cybersecurity, privacy, and data governance risks if appropriate safeguards are not in place. For example, AI applications may increase the risk of data leakage, unauthorized disclosure of sensitive information, inadequate employee access controls, or security vulnerabilities arising from improper configuration or integration with existing systems. An AI Acceptable Use Policy will establish clear governance standards governing the acquisition and use of AI technologies by setting forth requirements for the evaluation, approval, and secure use. The policy should reinforce compliance with existing cybersecurity policies and controls. Employees’ use of AI tools should be governed by the same standards and expectations that apply to all workplace conduct, including the organization’s Code of Conduct, information security policies, confidentiality obligations, and anti-harassment and equal employment opportunity policies. Providing employees with clear guidance on acceptable and prohibited uses of AI tools can help mitigate the risk of conduct that creates legal, compliance, or reputational exposure. For example, employers may wish to prohibit the use of AI tools to generate deepfakes or other deceptive synthetic media, impersonate colleagues, customers, or business partners, create discriminatory, harassing, or otherwise inappropriate communications, or engage in unauthorized business activities. Establishing clear guardrails can help reduce the likelihood that AI tools will be used in ways that violate workplace policies or applicable law.

news.titleEn: AI in the Empire State, Two Bills Could Create New Compliance Obligations
news.titleZh: 纽约州两项人工智能法案或带来新的合规义务
news.summaryZh: 纽约州两项待决法案可能对使用人工智能的组织施加新的通知和报告义务。两项法案均已通过州参议院和众议院，但截至2026年6月25日尚未由州长签署。第一项法案AB 3411B要求生成式人工智能系统的运营者在其用户界面上清晰显示输出可能不准确的声明，违反者每次违规最高可被处以1000美元民事罚款。第二项法案AB 9581B要求雇员超过50人或公开上市的企业向纽约州劳工部提交关于人工智能如何影响招聘和劳动力决策的年度报告。
news.bodyText: Find Your Next Job ! New York organizations using artificial intelligence should keep a close eye on two pending state bills that could create new notice and reporting obligations. Both bills have passed the Senate and Assembly, but as of June 25, 2026, neither appears to have been signed by the Governor. Still, they offer a clear signal that New York lawmakers are focused on transparency and workplace impact surrounding AI technologies. The first bill, AB 3411B, would amend the General Business Law to require notices on generative artificial intelligence systems. The second, AB 9581B, would amend the Labor Law to require certain businesses to submit annual reports to the New York Department of Labor about how AI affects hiring and workforce decisions. Note, taking a different approach to tracking AI-related job loss trends, California recently announced the California AI-Unemployment Tracker (CAIT), a public tracker based on unemployment insurance claims. Assembly Bill (AB) 3411B AB 3411B would apply to the owner, licensee, or operator of a generative AI system. The bill defines a generative AI system as a class of AI models that are “self-supervised” and “emulate input data to generate synthetic content, including text, images, videos, audio, and other digital content.” If enacted, the bill would require covered parties to “clearly and conspicuously” display a notice on the system’s user interface stating that outputs of the generative AI system may be inaccurate. Note the bill does not limit its reach to certain use cases, such as commercial or employment activities. The bill would take effect 90 days after becoming law. Organizations that develop, license, operate, or deploy generative AI systems for employees, applicants, customers, or the public may need to evaluate whether their user interfaces include the required notice. This may include chatbots, applicant-facing tools, customer service systems, document-drafting tools, or AI-enabled decision-support platforms. Failure to provide the required notice could result in a civil penalty of up to $1,000 per violation, with each user who does not receive the notice treated as a separate violation for each instance. Organizations using third-party AI tools should consider whether contracts clearly allocate responsibility for required notices, interface design, indemnification, and compliance updates. If this law is passed, it will take effect on the 90th day after it is signed. Assembly Bill (AB) 9581B AB 9581B is more directly tied to employment compliance. It would apply to a “covered business,” defined as a business entity doing business in New York that either employs more than 50 people or is publicly traded.

research.titleEn: BLAD: A Historically Contextualized, Multilingual Dataset of Bangladeshi Legal Acts (1799 to 2025)
research.titleZh: BLAD：孟加拉国法律法案的历史语境化多语言数据集（1799年至2025年）
research.abstractEn: We present the Bangladesh Legal Acts Dataset (BLAD), a curated collection of 1{,}484 legislative acts enacted between 1799 and 2025. Each act is represented with its full text, structured sections and footnotes, repeal status, and metadata linking it to the governing regime, head of state, and prevailing legal framework at the time of enactment. The corpus spans English, Bengali, and mixed-language documents, supporting temporal and multilingual analysis of statutory law. BLAD addresses a persistent gap in legal natural language processing (NLP) resources for low-resource, civil-law jurisdictions in South Asia. We describe the acquisition and enrichment pipeline, report descriptive statistics over more than two centuries of legislation, and outline the research directions the corpus enables. The dataset is publicly available under the CC~BY-SA~4.0 license at https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/sakhadib/bangladesh-legal-acts-dataset.
research.abstractZh: 我们介绍了孟加拉国法律法案数据集（BLAD），这是一个精选的集合，包含1799年至2025年间颁布的1,484项立法法案。每项法案都包含其全文、结构化的章节和脚注、废止状态，以及将其与颁布时的执政政权、国家元首和现行法律框架联系起来的元数据。该语料库涵盖英语、孟加拉语和混合语言文档，支持对成文法进行时间和多语言分析。BLAD填补了南亚低资源大陆法系司法管辖区法律自然语言处理（NLP）资源的长期空白。我们描述了采集和丰富流程，报告了超过两个世纪立法的描述性统计，并概述了该语料库所支持的研究方向。该数据集在CC BY-SA 4.0许可下公开可用，网址为https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/sakhadib/bangladesh-legal-acts-dataset。

news.summaryZh:

对诉讼律师而言，需关注不仅决定性裁决，还有程序性进展，如管辖权争议、禁令动议、集体认证和上诉动议，这些中期步骤在案件早期就能改变谈判筹码。对法务部门，当前新闻周期凸显法律、合规和沟通团队协调的重要性。重大法律事件发生后，首要问题往往是实务性的：是否影响合同、披露、政策或储备？是否需要重新审视文件保留、员工指导或监管沟通？合规团队应认识到执法趋势很少局限于单一行业，一个案件中的新理论可能迅速成为其他领域的模板。法律专业人士应将重大法律新闻视为早期预警系统，最关键的案例往往从渐进程序或调查进展开始，最终演变为先例、处罚或模仿诉讼。7月17-18日的周期之所以重要，不仅因为个别案件，更因为它展示了法律风险如何在各论坛间快速迁移。

news.titleEn: From “Service Improvement” to AI Exploitation: How Customer-Side Counsel Should Manage Vendor Data-Use Clauses
news.titleZh: 从“服务改进”到AI利用：客户方律师应如何管理供应商数据使用条款
news.summaryZh: HubSpot近期试图扩大客户CRM数据使用范围以支持AI功能，虽迅速撤回，但凸显了技术供应商将通用数据使用语言转化为AI开发许可的趋势。客户方律师需警惕，在AI时代，“服务改进”等概念可能被解释为授权训练AI系统或利用客户数据增强产品，尤其是当数据涉及CRM、客户名单等商业敏感信息时。首要任务是精确区分数据类别，明确供应商数据许可仅限于提供服务所需，未经同意不得用于AI训练。同时应审查“聚合”或“去标识化”数据条款，防止供应商提取价值。此外，需控制合同流程，警惕通过超链接条款单方面更改数据使用权。总之，传统协议中的广泛数据权利在AI背景下风险显著，需重新审视目的限制、二次使用及合同控制。
news.bodyText: Find Your Next Job ! HubSpot’s recent and quickly reversed attempt to expand its use of customer CRM data to support a new AI-powered lead-generation feature and potentially share certain customer data elements across its platform is the latest example of a broader contracting issue facing enterprise customers: technology vendors are increasingly seeking to convert general data-use language into permission to develop AI features, train or improve models, and, in some cases, create value across their customer base using data contributed by individual customers. For customer-side counsel, the lesson is not limited to one vendor or one product category. It is that familiar SaaS concepts, such as “service improvement,” “analytics,” and “product development,” can take on very different meanings in the AI era if they are not carefully constrained. Historically, many customers accepted broad vendor rights to use their data “to provide, maintain, support, and improve” the service. Before AI, that language was often understood to cover ordinary operational needs, such as debugging, security monitoring, and performance optimization. Today, however, those same words may be read to authorize training AI systems, building new features from patterns in customer data, generating cross-customer insights, or otherwise using one customer’s data to enhance the vendor’s broader product offering. That risk becomes especially acute where the relevant data is not merely technical telemetry, but substantive business information. CRM data, customer lists, pipeline details, pricing history, contract status, and sales strategy are often among a company’s most commercially sensitive assets. Even when public disclosure is not in play, many customers will object to a vendor using that information in ways that help other customers, improve generally available AI functionality, or otherwise dilute the competitive value of the underlying data set. The first priority for customer-side counsel, therefore, is to separate categories of data and rights with greater precision than many legacy technology agreements do. Customer content and business records should not be treated the same as usage metadata or service telemetry. Agreements should make clear that the vendor’s license to customer data is limited to what is necessary to provide the contracted services and related support, and not for broader product development or AI training purposes absent the customer’s affirmative agreement. Customer-side counsel should also examine provisions permitting use of “aggregated,” “anonymized,” or “de-identified” data. These are often framed as low-risk, but in practice they can give vendors wide latitude to extract value from customer data for secondary purposes. In many enterprise settings, the concern is not only whether data can be traced back to an individual company, but whether sensitive operational information is being used to improve the vendor’s products or create advantages for others in the market. The HubSpot experience also highlights the need to control the process, not just the substance. As we discussed in our previous post, vendors increasingly introduce AI-related changes through hyperlinked terms, privacy policies, feature notices, or product-specific terms rather than through negotiated amendments. Customer-side counsel should be wary of contractual structures that permit unilateral changes to data-use rights during the contract term, especially where those changes affect customer content, confidentiality expectations, or AI-related processing. Our next installment will examine ways to mitigate the impact of hyperlinked terms in preliminary vendor negotiations, including by making clear in the order-of-precedence clause that any hyperlinked, online, or other extra-contractual terms are subordinate to the negotiated agreement and cannot override its terms. The takeaway is straightforward: broad vendor rights that may have seemed benign in a traditional technology agreement can carry materially different risk once AI is in the picture. Data-use provisions and any applicable hyperlinked or extra-contractual terms deserve a fresh look, with particular care given to purpose limitation, secondary use, cross-customer benefit, and contractual controls on future updates to such terms. As vendors face competitive pressure and customer sensitivity around AI, many are willing to narrow data-use language when the issue is clearly framed. More Upcoming Events

news.titleEn: Will Businesses be Taxed for Using AI? Robot, Token and Floating Point Operations (FLOP) Taxes Explained
news.titleZh: 企业使用AI将被征税？机器人税、代币税与浮点运算税解析
news.summaryZh: 随着AI系统大规模替代人类员工执行任务，从起草文件到处理客户咨询，引发了关于就业替代和劳动所得税减少的经济担忧。政府可能面临因所得税损失而增加的财政压力，这重新激发了关于机器人税的兴趣，以及代币税和浮点运算税等替代方案的AI政策研究。机器人税旨在恢复人力和自动化劳动之间的税收中性，保留政府收入并用于再培训项目，但可能抑制技术投资。代币税直接对AI使用量征税，基于已追踪的计费代币，实施简单，但税负可能因模型效率不同而异。浮点运算税针对训练和运行AI所需的计算资源，欧盟AI法案已对超过特定计算阈值的通用AI模型实施安全控制。企业需理解这些税收提案，以制定有效的商业策略和税务规划。
news.bodyText: Find Your Next Job ! As AI systems continue to be adopted at scale, they are increasingly performing tasks carried out by human employees. From drafting documents, to writing code, to handling customer queries and concerns have grown about the economic risks this shift may pose, including job displacement and the erosion of the income taxes generated by human labour. This rapid automation of roles raises difficult questions around labour displacement, reduction and redeployment. A direct economic consequence of this is the growing fiscal pressure that governments may face due to loss of income tax. This has renewed interest in proposals for a robot tax, alongside the emergence of AI policy research on alternatives such as token tax and FLOP tax, each targeting a different point in the AI value chain: labour displacement, AI-driven usage and compute power. In short, as companies increase the pace and scale of AI adoption, there is an increasing likelihood that today’s efficiency gains will become tomorrow’s tax liabilities. Understanding if and how governments are proposing to tax AI deployment is therefore a new, but critical component of effective business strategy and tax planning. One potential economic consequence of businesses automating roles previously performed by human employees is a reduction in income tax revenues generated from labour. A key policy question is whether AI systems that perform tasks traditionally carried out by workers should be taxed as capital assets, rather than as a substitute for labour. Treating it as capital can create a tax-driven incentive for firms to replace human workers with automated systems, and a robot tax would eliminate this fiscal advantage and restore tax neutrality between human and automated labour. This would also prompt businesses to consider the real cost of labour replacement by weighing the benefits of human labour against automation. A robot tax can preserve government revenue that would otherwise be lost to automation and can be used to fund retraining programmes or unemployment support for displaced workers. However, taxing the use of machines can disincentivise investment in new technology, and the method of taxation would require a careful exercise of balancing labour interests with advancing innovation. Tokens are small units of data that come from breaking down whole words into parts of words, or punctuation, that AI models process language in. This is a computational unit, and not a linguistic one. AI providers typically use token-based pricing for AI models, with both inputs and outputs being chargeable. Unlike a robot tax, which targets labour substitution, a token tax would seek to capture value from AI usage directly, regardless of whether specific jobs are displaced. A token tax would be a levy applied to the provider’s billed token cost and may be simpler to implement as tokens are already tracked and billed by AI providers, making it a measurable proxy for AI-driven business activity. One of the challenges is that taxation may vary by model type. Models with less efficient architecture generate far more tokens for the same task than advanced models. The tax burden would depend heavily on which models a business happens to use rather than the value or complexity of the work performed. Significant computational resources are required to train and operate increasingly powerful models. The most capable AI systems depend on vast amounts of compute, measured in FLOPs. FLOP regulation is already within regulatory scope of the EU under the EU AI Act, whereby compute usage beyond a certain threshold would serve as a proxy for model-capability and trigger enhanced safety controls for general-purpose AI models that pose systemic risks.

research.titleEn: NOWJ@COLIEE 2026: Adaptive Pipelines for Legal Retrieval and Reasoning
research.titleZh: NOWJ@COLIEE 2026：用于法律检索与推理的自适应流水线
research.abstractEn: This paper presents the methodologies and results of the NOWJ team's participation across all five tasks of the COLIEE 2026 competition. For Task 1 (Legal Case Retrieval), we propose a four-stage pipeline comprising candidate filtering, dense retrieval with complementary embedding models, cross-encoder reranking via fine-tuned generative rerankers and MLP-based pairwise classification, and adaptive per-query cutoff prediction. For Task 2 (Legal Case Entailment), we combine BM25 filtering, T5-based reranking, and LLM-based entailment verification with consensus ensemble. For Task 3 (Statute Law Retrieval and Entailment), we adopt a retrieval-augmented generation framework with dense retrieval, attention-based reranking, and few-shot-prompted LLM reasoning. For Task 4 (Legal Textual Entailment), we introduce a dynamic routing pipeline that classifies query difficulty and dispatches cases to either a balanced few-shot solver or a structured zero-shot chain-of-thought solver. For the Pilot Task (Legal Judgment Prediction), we combine hierarchical transformers with CRF layers, argument relation mining, and probabilistic argumentation graph reasoning.
research.abstractZh: 本文介绍了NOWJ团队参加COLIEE 2026竞赛全部五项任务的方法和结果。对于任务1（法律案例检索），我们提出了一个四阶段流水线，包括候选过滤、使用互补嵌入模型的密集检索、通过微调生成式重排序器和基于MLP的成对分类进行交叉编码器重排序，以及自适应按查询截断预测。对于任务2（法律案例蕴含），我们结合了BM25过滤、基于T5的重排序和基于LLM的蕴含验证与共识集成。对于任务3（成文法检索与蕴含），我们采用了一种检索增强生成框架，包括密集检索、基于注意力的重排序和少样本提示的LLM推理。对于任务4（法律文本蕴含），我们引入了一种动态路由流水线，该流水线对查询难度进行分类，并将案例分派给平衡的少样本求解器或结构化的零样本思维链求解器。对于试点任务（法律判决预测），我们结合了层次化Transformer与CRF层、论据关系挖掘和概率论据图推理。

news.titleEn: Startup Corner: LexiTrove – AI for the employment matter lifecycle
news.titleZh: 创业角：LexiTrove——面向雇佣事务全生命周期的人工智能
news.summaryZh: 由Rohit Kumar和Rishabh Kumar兄弟于今年创立的LexiTrove，专注于英国雇佣法领域，构建围绕雇佣事务全生命周期的法律智能平台。该平台覆盖英国四个司法管辖区，结合工作流智能、ERA 2025对齐及特定司法管辖区的程序逻辑，为雇佣法律从业者提供从首次客户沟通到判决后的上下文感知协助。目前，LexiTrove正在招募首批雇佣法律事务所参与试点计划，以在产品商业发布前根据其工作流需求进行塑造。公司完全自筹资金，尚未进行外部融资。
news.bodyHtml:
Founded this year by brothers Rohit and Rishabh Kumar, LexiTrove is taking a specialist approach to legal AI and focusing exclusively on UK employment law. The startup is building its technology around the full employment matter lifecycle, incorporating the latest legislative changes. It’s early days and they are currently recruiting a founding cohort of employment law firms to help shape the platform ahead of its commercial launch, so if that sounds like you, take note.

How would you describe your company to a friend?

LexiTrove is a legal intelligence platform built specifically for employment law practitioners in the UK. It helps lawyers navigate the full lifecycle of an employment matter – from the first client conversation through to post-judgment by providing context-aware assistance throughout the matter.

Advertisement
And to a techy?

LexiTrove is a compliance-first legal intelligence platform engineered natively across all four UK jurisdictions. Built around the full employment matter lifecycle contentious, non-contentious and M&A it combines workflow intelligence, ERA 2025 alignment and jurisdiction specific procedural logic, designed from the ground up for employment practice, not retrofitted from a generic legal AI stack.

When were you founded?

14th May 2026

Advertisement
By who?

Rohit Kumar and Rishabh Kumar

Who are your key managers/senior execs?

LexiTrove is founded and run by Rohit Kumar and Rishabh Kumar.

Who are your target clients?

Solicitors, barristers and paralegals practising employment law across England & Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland.

What is your plan (growth strategy)?

We are currently onboarding a founding cohort of employment law firms and practitioners for a pilot programme, building the product directly around their workflow needs. The founding cohort gives practitioners an opportunity to shape the platform during development before our full commercial launch.

Key achievements?

We’ve mapped the employment matter lifecycle across all four UK jurisdictions, aligned our platform architecture with the Employment Rights Act 2025 and Employment Tribunal Procedure Rules 2024, launched our website and opened applications for our founding practitioner cohort.

Have you received investment?

No, LexiTrove is fully bootstrapped.

Have there been any key changes in direction since you were founded?

Not at this stage.

What are the key challenges in your market?

Employment law is one of the most procedurally complex areas of UK legal practice. Litigation volumes are rising, matter lifecycles are getting longer, and the Employment Rights Act 2025 has introduced the most significant legislative changes in a generation. Most legal technology is built for general practice and retrofitted for employment law LexiTrove is a platform built exclusively for this discipline from the ground up.

Tell us something people don’t already know about the company?

Rohit: We take our early consultation calls from the same room where I sat for my first job interview – and got selected. It feels less like a coincidence now and more like the room owes me a second win.

news.titleEn: FTC’s Caremark Insulin Settlement Puts PBM Rebate Practices in the Antitrust Crosshairs
news.titleZh: FTC与Caremark胰岛素和解案：PBM回扣实践成为反垄断焦点
news.summaryZh: 美国联邦贸易委员会（FTC）宣布与Caremark Rx和Zinc Health Services就胰岛素定价反垄断案达成和解，明确表明药房福利管理（PBM）回扣结构仍是执法重点。协议旨在降低患者自付费用、提高透明度，并遏制推高胰岛素标价的回扣做法。该案是FTC对PBM处方集、回扣及药物排位决策的广泛挑战的一部分，虽仅解决对Caremark和Zinc的指控，但行业影响深远。法律上，和解直指PBM激励结构，FTC认为回扣安排通过奖励高标价扭曲竞争，即使患者最终承担更高费用。若该理论获支持，药品供应链企业将面临对标准商业安排的更严格审查。此案标志着反垄断理论在医疗保健市场的演变，监管机构正审视中介补偿模式的反竞争效果。内部法律顾问和合规团队需重新评估回扣计划、处方集决策及定价策略文件，PBM、制造商和下游公司应关注透明度义务和回扣传递机制。和解表明FTC正围绕医疗可负担性和可及性构建反垄断法，其从主要PBM附属公司获得运营变更的能力将影响未来调查和谈判。
news.relevanceReason: 文章主要涉及FTC与PBM的和解及反垄断执法，核心是药品定价和PBM回扣实践，虽与法律监管相关，但并非直接聚焦法律AI或法律技术，而是更广泛的医疗保健反垄断议题。

news.titleEn: DOJ Draws Line on Unredacted Epstein Files Sought by New Mexico
news.titleZh: 司法部就新墨西哥州索要未删节爱泼斯坦文件划清界限
news.summaryZh: 美国司法部告知新墨西哥州官员，无法合法移交与杰弗里·爱泼斯坦相关的未删节文件，这些文件是州调查人员为调查爱泼斯坦前牧场相关行为而索要的。这一请求引发了联邦与州之间的显著争议，核心问题在于当法院强加的保密保护和受害者隐私权仍然有效时，合作能走多远。现有法律限制（包括保护令、对受害者和证人的隐私义务以及调查材料的限制）阻止了以新墨西哥州要求的形式披露文件。对于法律专业人士而言，这一争议的意义远超爱泼斯坦案本身，凸显了透明度要求与保密规则之间的冲突，尤其是在平行程序中。保护令对下游披露具有约束力，即使其他政府实体声称出于执法目的需要信息。公司内部法律顾问和合规团队也应关注此案，因为当公司收到多个监管机构的相同记录请求时，会出现类似的结构性问题。程序上，这场斗争可能取决于新墨西哥州能否通过更窄的请求或法院干预获取信息；实质上，它凸显了公共问责与保护受害者和调查完整性之间的紧张关系。
news.relevanceReason: 文章主要讨论联邦与州在调查文件披露上的法律争议，涉及保护令、隐私权和调查材料限制等法律问题，但核心并非直接关于法律AI或法律科技，而是法律程序与合规问题，因此相关性为中等。

news.titleEn: K&L Gates cuts circa 10% of its business services workforce
news.titleZh: K&L Gates裁减约10%业务服务人员
news.summaryZh: K&L Gates启动一轮重大裁员，针对其“联盟专业人员”队伍，裁减全球业务支持员工约10%。此次裁员不涉及律师和合伙人。经过数月全面结构审查，为更好适应当前业务运营并支持未来增长，决定减少联盟专业人员，以精简支持结构，确保满足客户即时需求并预测未来需求。事务所将为受影响员工提供离职补偿和再就业支持。上次大规模业务服务裁员发生在2017年，当时事务所因技术动荡暂停SAP项目转向Elite 3E。近12至24个月，多家大型律所因技术驱动运营效率而裁减业务服务人员，如Perkins Coie（2025年6月裁减5%）、Bryan Cave Leighton Paisner（2024年3月裁减约50个岗位，占8%）、Faegre Drinker Biddle & Reath（2024年7月裁减“少量”岗位，低于5%）、A&O Shearman（2026年5月裁减伦敦约20个业务服务岗位）。相比之下，K&L Gates此次10%的裁员幅度显著更深。
news.bodyHtml:
K&L Gates has launched a significant round of redundancies targeting its “allied professional” workforce, cutting roughly 10% of its global business support staff.

First picked up by Above the Law in the United States, the cuts do not affect lawyers and associates. In a statement sent to Legal IT Insider by K&L Gates, global managing partner Stacy Ackerman said: “Following a comprehensive, multi-month review of our structure to better align with how our business operates today and support future growth, we made the decision to reduce our allied professional workforce. This action is being taken to streamline our support structure, ensuring that we are attuned to immediate client needs and well positioned to anticipate and meet future demand. We are committed to supporting our people throughout this transition, including through separation benefits and outplacement support for impacted colleagues. Our focus remains on serving our clients with the excellence, responsiveness, and expertise they have come to expect from our firm.”

Advertisement

The last time we’re aware that there were big business services layoffs at the firm was 2017, coinciding with a turbulent period in the firm’s tech history, when the firm shelved its SAP project in favour of Elite 3E.

K&L Gates is far from an isolated case. Over the past 12 to 24 months, several major law firms have quietly or overtly trimmed their business services staff as technology drives operational efficiency:

Advertisement

  • Perkins Coie (June 2025): Laid off 5% of its business professional staff following a comprehensive, year-long structural review.

  • Bryan Cave Leighton Paisner (March 2024): Eliminated approximately 50 business services roles (8%) of professional staff across its US and UK offices.

  • Faegre Drinker Biddle & Reath (July 2024): Conducted a “small number” of operations support roles cuts representing “less than 5%”

  • A&O Shearman (May 2026): Cut about 20 business services roles in London, impacting non-legal staff across IT, finance and marketing.

However, by comparison, this 10% cuts significantly deeper than some of the other recent redundancy drives.

news.titleEn: From models to solutions: What Anthropic’s Ode launch signals for legal
news.titleZh: 从模型到解决方案：Anthropic推出Ode对法律行业意味着什么
news.summaryZh: Anthropic、黑石集团和Hellman & Friedman正式推出AI服务公司Ode，该公司结合Anthropic的前沿AI模型与工程师及运营团队，并获得高盛、General Atlantic、Leonard Green & Partners、Apollo Global Management、GIC和Sequoia Capital等投资者支持。Ode基于2026年5月收购的Fractional AI组建，由Fractional AI联合创始人Chris Taylor和Eddie Siegel分别担任CEO和CTO。许多组织虽认识到AI潜力，但难以将其转化为运营成果，Ode将与客户合作定义并执行高优先级AI计划。AI下一波浪潮在于重塑特定行业工作流程的垂直解决方案。他于2025年7月创立法律产品工作室Purple，帮助律所将创意转化为按结果定价的平台。律所自建项目显著增加，如Kirkland & Ellis与Palantir合作投入5亿美元开发AI，Shoosmiths推出合同审查平台Apollo。律所正从主流法律AI工具转向针对特定工作流程的AI应用。Ode对法律行业的直接相关性可能取决于律所规模和预算，但服务驱动的AI采用预计将进一步增长。
news.bodyHtml:
This week Anthropic, Blackstone and Hellman & Friedman officially launched Ode, an AI services company that combines Anthropic’s frontier AI models with a team of engineers and operators, backed by a consortium of heavyweight investors that includes Goldman Sachs, General Atlantic, Leonard Green & Partners, Apollo Global Management, GIC and Sequoia Capital.

The launch is built on the foundation of Fractional AI, the applied AI services firm acquired in May 2026. Fractional AI’s team, alongside engineers from Anthropic, forms the operational core of the new business. Ode is led by Fractional AI co-founders Chris Taylor and Eddie Siegel, who assume the roles of chief executive officer and chief technology officer respectively.

Announcing the launch, Taylor said that while organisations increasingly recognise AI’s potential, many continue to struggle to translate that potential into operational outcomes. “Our teams partner closely with CEOs and across organisations to define and execute the highest priority AI initiatives,” he said. “By pairing the deep subject matter expertise of our clients with our top applied AI talent, we’re able to drive transformation-level impact.”

Advertisement

Some may read this as Anthropic becoming frustrated that they are not seeing faster progress in organisations leveraging their technology for organisational change.

For law firms, the launch is notable because it reflects the fact, as noted by legal AI founder Tim Pullan in welcoming the launch of Ode, that the next wave of AI is not just in the models, it’s in vertical solutions that reshape workflows and offerings for specific industries. Pullan founded law firm product studio Purple in July 2025, with the aim of helping law firms to ‘turn ideas into outcome-priced platforms that clients value.’

Advertisement

We have already seen a marked increase in law firm build projects, not least Kirkland & Ellis’s $500m AI build with Palantir. Shoosmiths in June launched its own contract review platform Apollo, which it would be surprising if it didn’t productise.

In a post on LinkedIn this week, Pullan said that in founding Purple, “We bet that the most ambitious law firms wouldn’t stop at ‘AI-enabled drafting’, workflow fixes or internal copilots. They would use the speed, power and flexibility of AI to do something bigger; turn hard-won service expertise into products, shift from manual advisory to productised offerings, and build client experiences that simply weren’t possible in the pre-AI age. Importantly, these products will become significant engines of scale and profit (not ‘cheap law’).

Speaking to Legal IT Insider, Pullan observed: “If law firms are investing in building their own version of a tool that is widely available in the market the business case is harder than if they build to redefine their offering with a tool that is client facing.”

Legal tech software developer Xperate, set up by former Tikit heads Simon Hill and Mark Garnish five years ago to help law firms with their own builds, echo that this is the direction of travel. Hill told Legal IT Insider: “Xperate is working with both legal vendors and law firms on phase two of the AI revolution; we’re moving into very specific workflows to solve legal workflow issues. We’ve been invited by a top 20 global law firm onto their AI strategy group because they have trialled mainstream legal AI tools and now want to apply AI to specific workflows within teams to solve issues they have at a practical level. That is where things are moving to.”

Whether Ode becomes directly relevant to legal probably depends on how big your law firm is and what your budget is. There is also a query over the extent to which generalist engineers and operators can really understand and work with law firms to squeeze the most out of their specialist knowledge.

That aside, we can expect to see further growth in services-led AI adoption, as organisations increasingly look for specialist expertise to translate advances in foundation models into measurable business outcomes.

We’ve been invited by a top 20 global law firm onto their AI strategy group because they have trialled mainstream legal AI tools and now want to apply AI to specific workflows within teams to solve issues they have at a practical level. That is where things are moving to.” Whether Ode becomes directly relevant to legal probably depends on how big your law firm is and what your budget is. There is also a query over the extent to which generalist engineers and operators can really understand and work with law firms to squeeze the most out of their specialist knowledge. That aside, we can expect to see further growth in services-led AI adoption, as organisations increasingly look for specialist expertise to translate advances in foundation models into measurable business outcomes.

news.titleZh: Paxton AI 推出安全案件协作功能，为诉讼团队提供最先进的情报共享方式
news.summaryZh: Paxton AI 宣布推出 Secure Matter Collaboration 新功能，允许多名律师在同一律所内安全协作处理诉讼案件。团队可在共享工作区上传文件、构建案件时间线、审查证据、起草诉状、发现文件及庭审准备材料，取代分散的电子邮件链和重复上传。该功能解决了诉讼中常见的团队协作碎片化问题，避免重复劳动和过时工作产品带来的风险。每位协作者使用个人账户登录，案件访问权限由中央管理并符合律所道德墙要求，消除了凭证共享和重复上传的弊端。当前支持医疗账单摘要、动议、时间线和案件草稿等生成内容的协作，更多协作功能正在规划中。该功能使团队所有授权成员无需共享凭证或重复工作即可使用相同文件、时间线、证据和工作产品，从而加快办案速度、提高协作效率并降低信息遗漏风险。
news.bodyHtml:
This new collaboration feature lets multiple attorneys at a firm securely work the same case together — sharing files, chronologies, evidence, and drafts in one workspace instead of scattered email chains and duplicate uploads

San Francisco, California — July 17, 2026 — Paxton AI, the AI litigation platform for legal research, document drafting, and case analysis, today announced Secure Matter Collaboration, a new capability that enables multiple attorneys at the same firm to securely collaborate on a litigation matter. Teams can upload files, build case chronologies, review evidence, and draft briefs, discovery documents, and trial preparation materials – all within a shared, secure workspace.

The release addresses one of litigation’s most persistent operational challenges: keeping multiple attorneys aligned as a matter evolves. Files, chronologies, research, and drafts often become fragmented across email, shared drives, and individual workspaces, leading to duplicate effort, outdated work product, and unnecessary risk.

“Being able to collaborate using the same set of matter documents is a game changer,” said Ashley King Owner of Crown Discovery. “With other tools, attorneys may have to create separate workspaces and upload the same documents again. Paxton gives the entire team access to the same files and matter intelligence while still allowing each person to work independently. That is much closer to how litigation teams actually need to operate.”

 

Shared Access Respecting Ethical Walls

Secure Matter Collaboration gives every attorney added to a matter immediate access to the same case files and generated outputs — no re-uploading, no forwarding attachments, no waiting on whoever happens to hold the account. Each collaborator signs in under their own individual account, while access to the matter itself is managed centrally and in line with the firm’s ethical walls, eliminating the credential-sharing and duplicate-upload problems that slow teams down.

 

Key capabilities include:

  • Shared matter access. Every team member works from the same evidence, chronology, research, and case files — not separate copies that quietly drift apart.
  • One workspace instead of email chains. Uploading files, building chronologies, reviewing evidence, and drafting legal documents all happen directly in Paxton.• Individual accounts, centralized access. Attorneys use their own logins while matter-level access is managed by the firm, respecting ethical walls and removing the need to share credentials.
  • Review without overwriting. Teammates can review each other’s drafts and outputs without risk of overwriting one another’s work.
  • Faster approvals. Shared visibility into a matter’s current state means faster sign-off to file-ready output.
  • Enterprise-grade security. Collaboration is protected by enterprise-grade security, and documents and data are never used to train Paxton’s AI models.

 

The feature currently supports collaboration on medical billing summaries, motions, and other generated artifacts including chronologies and case drafts, with additional collaboration capabilities on the roadmap.

“Litigation is a team effort, but most legal AI software still treats a matter as though it belongs to one person,” said Tanguy Chau, Ph.D., CEO and Founder of Paxton AI. “We built Secure Matter Collaboration so every authorized member of a litigation team can work from the same files, chronologies, evidence, and work product without sharing credentials or recreating work. When the entire team has a common understanding of the matter, attorneys can move faster, collaborate more effectively, and reduce the risk of important information falling through the cracks.”

 

Availability

Secure Matter Collaboration is available now to Paxton customers. Full documentation is available on Paxton’s website.

 

About Paxton AI

Paxton AI is the AI platform built for Litigation teams, combining legal research, document drafting, and case analysis in one place. Paxton’s research tools surface on-point case law, statutes, and regulations at the state, federal, and appellate level, with a citation on every answer and an AI Citator that flags whether a case is still good law. Paxton is SOC 2, ISO 27001, and HIPAA compliant, and customer data is never used to train its AI models. Learn more at www.paxton.ai.

Dora Yun

650-392-2831

Dora@paxton.ai
