news.titleEn: Startups Are Pushing to Democratize Legal Research. Will They Succeed?
news.titleZh: 初创公司推动法律研究民主化，它们能成功吗？
news.summaryZh:
法律研究初创公司正致力于让法律研究更易获取且成本更低，部分公司甚至向更广泛的法律科技市场提供其专有判例法数据库以支持创新。Midpage 和 Descrybe 等初创公司通过提供低价订阅服务（如 Descrybe 每月 75 美元）和向其他平台集成数据来扩大访问。然而，法律研究市场此前经历了显著整合，例如 Fastcase 与 vLex 合并后被 Clio 收购，LexisNexis 收购 Lex Machina 和 Ravel Law，以及 Thomson Reuters 收购 Casetext 并起诉 ROSS。2025 年底，Clio 旗下的 Fastcase 起诉 Alexi 未经授权使用其数据库，导致 Alexi 大幅裁员。

尽管存在整合风险，但一些观察者认为当前环境不同：风险投资对法律科技的兴趣增加，以及 Free Law Project 和 Caselaw Access Project 等资源为初创公司提供了更长的生存期。初创公司还通过添加法规和规章来扩展业务，如 Abstract 利用生成式 AI 提供监管洞察。法律研究的创新永无止境，而 Ed Walters 则认为市场可能由更多机构参与者主导，但历史不一定会重演。
news.bodyHtml:
These newcomers are looking to make legal research more accessible and inexpensive for attorneys, with some even offering their proprietary built case law databases to the broader legal technology market to support innovation.

While such efforts are welcomed by those striving to make case law accessible, the push to democratize legal research may only be able to go so far. For instance, some see the risk of these efforts being stifled in an industry where mergers and acquisitions have been the norm. Others, however, argue that past isn’t always prologue and believe the new crop of startups may be around for much longer than their predecessors.

More Data, More Access

While it has become easier to build primary law databases thanks to advances in artificial intelligence, for many startups making this information more accessible is just beginning.
Legal research startup Midpage’s business model, for instance, is built on ensuring the industry has access to its legal research database.

“Instead of just focusing on being any old research company, we also integrate this data into many other platforms and make it more accessible, … so we're now sort of filling that gap that Fastcase used to fill,” Midpage founder and CEO Otto von Zastrow told Law.com.

He added that the startup has “revenue share relationships” with legal tech companies, including Litera, that add Midpage’s legal research capabilities to their core platforms. Midpage is also providing data to at least one other legal research company.

“We absolutely have legal research companies that have reached out, and we have one of them that we have already given access to. … For us, it's already bigger business to be the infrastructure and the data provider than to only go to law firms,” von Zastrow said.

Like Midpage, legal research startup Descrybe also looks to promote access to its legal research database. The company began in the access-to-justice space before pivoting to focus on legal organizations.

The startup’s CEO and co-founder Kara Peterson told Law.com that while Descrybe caters to Big Law clients similar to most other legal research providers, it also targets “solo, smaller, midsize [firms], legal aid [organizations], in-house teams, nonprofits, students, researchers, all of that.”

Descrybe has kept its prices low to cater to a market that might not need the more extensive—and expensive—platforms offered by the established legal research players. “If you're smaller, that's just over-engineering for what they need, and they don't necessarily want to pay for all those pieces that they don't need. So there is a real space for solutions that solve problems, and it's $75 a month.”

These startups’ push to make legal research more accessible comes after a period of significant consolidation in the legal research market, which limited the availability of case law data.

Fastcase, which licenses legal research data to other startups, for instance, merged with fellow legal research company vLex in 2023, while the combined entity—named the vLex group—was acquired by practice management software provider Clio in 2025.

Meanwhile, LexisNexis acquired Lex Machina in 2015 and Ravel Law in 2017. The latter acquisition impacted the Caselaw Access Project, an initiative launched by Harvard Law School that aimed to publicly release digital scans of 40 million pages of state and federal court decisions, pushing back its release from 2017 to 2024.

Likewise, Thomson Reuters changed the market with its 2023 acquisition of Casetext—the startup that created the now well-known CoCounsel platform.

Years before, Thomson Reuters also sued legal research startup ROSS in 2020, in an ongoing lawsuit alleging copyright infringement, which saw a partial summary judgement last year. ROSS shut down its operations in December 2020.

To be sure, that is not the only industry lawsuit impacting a legal research startup. In late 2025, Clio-owned Fastcase sued legal research startup Alexi for alleged unauthorized use of its case law database in order to build its own platform, a claim that Alexi has vigorously pushed back on. Due to the ongoing litigation, Alexi has shrunk its head count considerably.

Is Past Prologue?

While the growth of new startups in the legal research market is a welcome development for many, there are concerns over whether efforts to democratize this space will be stifled by yet another wave of consolidation.

“I want there to be a diverse field of competing organizations driving the price down, making powerful tools available to the public. But, if [legacy legal research companies] just keep buying everybody as soon as they get big enough, we're not making progress,” said Michael Lissner, co-founder and executive director of the Free Law Project, a nonprofit that provides access to its own developed primary law database.

“That may happen, it's pretty hard to say no to their money, especially if ... you're startup with investors and your investors want to get paid out,” he added. “Organizations get big enough, they get bought and consolidate. So, it’s like, expand for a while and then shrink.”

While always a possibility, more consolidations are not a certainty. Though the legal research market was ripe for M&A in the recent past, some argue the current situation is much different.

“One of the challenges we've had in the past is not consolidation, it's that startups simply ran out of money,” said Ed Walters, co-founder of Fastcase and vice president, legal innovation and strategy at Clio. “And one major structural change in this market right now is that their legal tech has become sexy to venture [capital] firms, and there's more investment in the space than there ever was. So that will sustain startups, I think, for longer than they were able to in the past.”

Walters also noted there are more resources to foster and sustain startups, pointing to the Free Law Project and the culmination of the Caselaw Access Project. “It’s not something that gets stuffed back into a bottle somehow. That will always exist. I think those are very powerful in fertilizing the ground for new entrants in the market.”

To be sure, the startups in the market are also aiming to democratize access to other types of primary law besides just court opinions—expanding their focus beyond just the legal research space. Midpage and Descrybe, for instance, are adding statutes and regulations to their platforms, joining other new startups in the regulatory space, including Abstract which leverages gen AI to alert clients and provide actionable insights on proposed regulations and laws.

Such broadened appeal may give newcomers new revenue streams and clients, and essentially more staying power in the market.

Just how much, however, is a matter of debate. Some, like Walters, don’t see history repeating itself, but instead the emergence of broader market dominated by more established players. “This may not be a short story. It might be a long story. … There are more institutional players all the time.”

Yet even if another consolidation wave were to shrink the legal research market again—and hinder access to case law—it may not be too long before another crop of startups arise. The push to innovate legal research, it seems, is never complete.

“While democratizing legal research and creating systems that are affordable will be a motivation for some, and will be the business strategy for some, I also think that legal research is something where you're never finished,” said Pablo Arredondo, co-founder of legal research startup Casetext, and former vice president, CoCounsel at Thomson Reuters. “It’s the relentless pursuit of better ways to navigate the common law, faster, more intuitive ways to surface what's needed.”

news.titleZh: 汤森路透在密歇根州因研究平台显示社保数据遭隐私集体诉讼
news.summaryZh: 汤森路透美国公司于周四遭遇集体诉讼，被指控违反密歇根州隐私法，在其CLEAR和Westlaw PeopleMap平台上公开显示个人社会安全号码的连续五位数字。
news.bodyText: Thomson Reuters America Corp. was hit with a class action Thursday that accused it of breaching a Michigan state privacy law by publicly displaying five sequential digits of individuals’ Social Security numbers on its CLEAR and Westlaw PeopleMap platforms.

news.titleEn: The New Era For Legal Tech Begins
news.titleZh: 法律科技新时代开启
news.summaryZh: 微软进入合同审查领域标志着法律科技行业新时代的开始，预计将引发用户行为转变。大语言模型估算显示，一旦Legal Agent和Claude for Word广泛可用，18%至25%的大型律所律师将放弃专业工具。内部法律团队和中小型律所受到的影响可能更大。对于尚未深度使用法律AI工具、且工作风险等级不高的律师而言，使用已嵌入日常办公流程且成本更低的工具是自然选择。微软套件（包括Copilot）的普及将使Legal Agent的采用门槛降低。小型律所、中型律所、处理日常合同需求的内部团队以及尚未全面引入法律AI平台的ALSPs将率先转移。而大型律所和大型内部团队因已投入专业法律AI工具且对成本不敏感，受影响较小。专注于文档审查的法律科技公司将面临最大冲击，其总可寻址市场将大幅缩减。合同审查专业公司受影响最严重，CLM平台也受到显著冲击。法律科技公司需通过创新和构建差异化功能来保持竞争力，否则将被微软和Anthropic侵蚀市场。此外，这一趋势将加速计时收费模式的消亡，并改变客户预期。
news.bodyHtml:
Microsoft’s entry into contract review* marks the beginning of a new era for the sector. It also marks a likely shift of user behaviour, with LLM-generated estimates suggesting between 18% and 25% of large firm lawyers leaving specialist tools for the new Legal Agent, or Claude for Word, once they are widely available.

For the inhouse and small-to-medium size firm segments the impact is even more likely to be felt strongly. See charts below. The blue one is via ChatGPT and the ochre one is Claude. They were asked to consider what % of lawyers would move away from specialised legal tech tools for doc review, if Legal Agent and Claude for Word were widely available.

What Does This Mean?

One thing that struck AL is that the results are not that different to the estimated impact of Claude – with the Word add-in and all possible tooling – that this site considered before.

Why is that? The reason is that the trigger and the pathway to move away from legal tech is often the same. If you are not committed to legal AI tools already, and the work you do is not always ‘bet the $1 billion company’ scale or risk level, then tools that easily live within the way you work already – and cost a lot less than some legal tech offerings – is really not a big step.

Most lawyers will have the Microsoft suite, including Copilot. If and when Legal Agent becomes universal – even if there are some small additional costs – the decision to use it, if it works well in the real world, will be easy to make.

So, small firms, medium size firms, those within inhouse teams that are mostly focused on day to day contract needs, and those ALSPs that have not yet fully brought in one of the legal AI platforms to work with, are those who will shift over. And some will be doing so already with regard to Claude.

Conversely – and AL has explored this in depth several times in relation to Claude – Big Law and large inhouse teams, especially those handling very high risk matters – will be both 1) already committed to a range of legal AI tools that provide doc review, whether as their main feature or as an additional feature, and 2) where cost of legal tech tools is not a big issue, especially when those tools come with a much broader offering that covers specialised workflows and curated legal data.

Hence the clear patterns we see above and have seen before in AL analyses.

Impact

Any legal tech tool that is focused primarily on doc review gets impacted here. While they will hold onto many of their Big Law customers, possibly by building a moat with new features, perhaps around data curation, their TAM will take a big hit.

Companies that have been hoping to expand revenue by selling into the smaller firm market, or inhouse world, will soon run up against the hard to argue point that Legal Agent and/or Claude for Word ‘is simpler and cheaper’ – at least for their needs.

This may affect the valuations of all legal tech companies. The specialist contract companies clearly get hit the most. But, even large platforms that venture into contract review will have some of their TAM cut away. CLM also gets hit hard.

As ever, and as AL has said before, the way ahead is therefore to innovate, to build new features that stand out and allow you to keep winning hearts and minds. Sitting still means having Microsoft and Anthropic eat away at your TAM. And they will likely only get better at doing it.

Conclusion

One last thing: this also impacts the legal market directly. If it becomes globally easier for all firms, and all clients, to speed through document review – a key pillar of the market’s activity – then how does this change the legal world as a whole?

For AL, it’s another nail in the billable hour coffin for routine law firm work, as selling your value by time alone will mean you are poorer. And for clients the realisation that you can use AI to really zoom through such work will become universal, which will help them, and change expectations.

Plus, how long before Google, or Meta, or someone else in the Big Tech world decides that after seeing all the exciting news about legal AI and the revenue they can make there – no doubt helped by spotting movie star adverts everywhere – that they should ‘do legal tech’ as well? All bets are off now.

Welcome to the new era of legal tech.

Richard Tromans, Founder, Artificial Lawyer, May 1st, 2026

Note * – in early 2015, Microsoft bought Equivio, which was a text analytics startup used in eDiscovery. It was absorbed into the company’s wider information governance offering and appears not to have had much of a meaningful impact. One can say that the Robin AI team that joined MS, were hired in part in order to help the tech giant to provide a distinct legal tech offering. Many thanks to Ed Walters for reminding AL of the 2015 move. For what it’s worth AL started in the summer of 2016 🙂

But, first up, how to get your free ticket to attend the Legal Innovators conferences in Europe, Paris – June 24 and 25, and also California, San Francisco – June 10 and 11. Legal Innovators has grown and grown, we do more conferences now globally, and the events are getting much, much larger as well. At present we are focusing on the upcoming Legal Innovators conferences in Europe, Paris – June 24 and 25, and also California, San Francisco – June 10 and 11. (There will be a New York and a London conference this November as well.)

Click on the images, or links, below and you will be taken to the Express Registration page. Express route to your Legal Innovators California June 10th and 11th ticket here.

Legal Innovators California, the landmark West Coast legal tech event, will take place on June 10 and 11, in the heart of the Bay Area, the home to many of the world’s leading AI businesses – and plenty of legal tech pioneers as well! More information and tickets here.

—

OK, after this week it’s hard to focus on anything else other than how much the market will eventually be shaken up by Claude and Microsoft, but, here is a collection of other news – which AL will keep brief.

Meet Mexican NewMod HAA Legal

HAA Legal is based in Monterrey, Mexico, and is the ‘only AI-native patrimonial architecture firm operating under civil law in the Spanish-speaking world, currently live in production – built without external capital’, they said.

‘The firm runs a proprietary operating system of twenty-plus specialized agents covering structural design, adversarial review, and institutional drafting across trusts, holdings, family governance and private capital. Twenty-one years of senior patrimonial practice, now encoded and running under Mexican law,’ they added.

–

Newcode + TR Deep Research

US law firm Robinson+Cole has integrated Thomson Reuters’ Deep Research directly into Newcode.ai, the agentic AI platform implemented last year to support legal workflows across practices.

The addition of Deep Research allows attorneys to:

  • Perform sophisticated legal research using agentic workflows that mirror real world legal reasoning
  • Receive structured, verifiable responses grounded in Thomson Reuters data
  • Streamline research processes while maintaining rigorous quality and accuracy standards
  • Work entirely within Robinson+Cole’s firm controlled AI environment.

—

Meet Lawgic From Greece

Lawgic is a Greek legal AI company built by lawyer Panos Karachalios. It handles a range of skills.

  • Legal translation built on EU legal dictionaries  
  • Amendment tracking for both Greek and EU law  
  • A Regulatory and compliance layer for General Counsel is also coming soon.

—

And also:

  • Harvey has opened an office in Chicago, adding to its rapidly expanding global footprint.
  • Eversheds Sutherland has hired Kenzo Tsushima to lead the Legal Managed Services practice for Konexo US, expanding its capacity to help corporate legal departments tackle high-volume work through AI-enabled delivery and process optimization. He had previously worked at Epiq.
  • Herbert Smith Freehills Kramer has appointed Lisa McLaughlin as Managing Partner of Digital Legal Delivery.
  • Raymond Blyd’s departure didn’t last long and Legalcomplex is now back. The ‘new version ships AI Research Chat grounded in seven years of original research (139 blog posts, 112 market maps), and a fresh Spark MCP server that connects 31,000+ legal tech companies to any MCP-compatible agent’, he said.
  • Anaqua has acquired Patrix, an IP management software and services business.
  • Questel, also in IP, has announced the release of QaECTER, a new AI model for patent search.
  • Minerva, the intelligent client onboarding for law firms, has announced a new strategic partnership with Thirdfort, the client due diligence platform.
  • Litera has hired legal tech veteran Grant Hewlett to lead its AI Firm Intelligence Portfolio.
  • Definely has launched an MCP capability that ‘enables real-time, secure connectivity between Definely’s specialist contract review tools and the enterprise AI environments lawyers are already using’.
  • Spellbook has launched an integration with iManage.

—

And now some videos:

AL TV Product Walk Through – Chamelio

—

AL TV Product Walk Through – Opus 2

–

And that’s all folks. Have a great weekend!

As mentioned, there is a Bank Holiday in the UK on Monday, so AL will be back on Tuesday May 5th.

And if you’d like to join some of the leading legal innovation speakers and legal tech companies in the world, in California, or Paris, this June, then check out the Express Registration above.

Richard Tromans, Founder, Artificial Lawyer.

news.titleEn: Definely launches MCP and says “don’t ask AI to check itself”
news.titleZh: Definely推出MCP，称“不要让AI自我审查”
news.summaryZh: 合同技术公司Definely推出模型上下文协议（MCP），使律师能在企业AI环境中直接调用Definely的专业审查工具。随着AI生成文件数量激增，专家判断至关重要，而让AI自我审查并非解决方案。MCP通过提供客观、确定性的审查基线，弥补这一差距。Definely将合同视为结构化对象，MCP利用其工具产生可重复结果，且输出可审计，这是生成式模型无法做到的。生成式AI可受益于结构化分析工具，MCP连接企业AI平台与结构化审查工具，提供可验证的事实。Troutman Pepper Locke已在其企业AI代理Athena中部署Definely，其创新解决方案总监Max Gladstone称，MCP将推动更无缝、互联的法律技术工作流程。
news.bodyHtml:
Definely – the contract technology company used by law firms and in-house teams including A&O Shearman, Slaughter and May, Troutman Pepper Locke, Samsung and KPMG – has launched a Model Context Protocol (MCP), enabling lawyers to call Definely’s specialist review tools from directly inside their enterprise AI environments.

As the volume of AI-generated drafting threatens to outstrip the speed of human review, expert judgement has never been more critical, and asking an AI to check itself should not be a solution for clients, risk committees and courts. Definely says that its MCP closes this gap by equipping lawyers with an objective, deterministic baseline for review. Definely treats contracts as structured objects. The MCP uses Definely’s tools to deliver repeatable results and the output is auditable in a way that a generative model’s review of its own work cannot be.

Advertisement

“Generative AI can benefit from tools offering structured analysis, much like the way they might use a calculator tool for maths,” said Shima Rashidi, head of AI at Definely. “The Definely MCP connects Enterprise AI platforms to our structured review tools, allowing the AI to report verifiable facts, providing the repeatable and auditable results that human accountability demands in the legal sector.”

The calculator analogy is deliberately chosen. Just as a language model should not be trusted to perform arithmetic from first principles when a calculator is available, Definely argues it should not be trusted to validate its own structural outputs when a purpose-built tool can do it with certainty.

Advertisement

Troutman Pepper Locke, which has deployed Definely alongside its proprietary Enterprise AI agent Athena, welcomed the MCP launch, with Max Gladstone, director of innovation solutions, observing: “With near-universal adoption of Athena, our Enterprise AI agent, Troutman Pepper Locke continues to build strong momentum in leveraging AI to drive better client outcomes and improved attorney experience. Our partnership with Definely and their MCP advances that effort, enabling more seamless, connected workflows across the legal technology landscape.”

news.titleEn: Linda Henry Joins iManage as Vice President of Customer Success
news.titleZh: Linda Henry 加入 iManage 担任客户成功副总裁
news.summaryZh: iManage 宣布 Linda Henry 加入公司担任客户成功副总裁，负责领导全球客户成功团队。Henry 将致力于构建更主动、价值驱动的客户成功模式，重点加强跨职能协作、运营一致性，并将 AI 能力融入客户支持流程。她将领导一支 50 人的全球团队，优化运营模式和分层策略，并强化与销售、支持、市场、产品等部门的协作。Henry 此前在 Salesforce、Google、AWS 和 Microsoft 等科技公司积累了丰富经验，专注于规模化客户团队和全球业务增长。她将向 iManage 客户体验执行副总裁 James Priz 汇报。
news.bodyHtml:
New leader to help scale a more proactive, value-driven customer success organization aligned to adoption, retention, and growth

 

CHICAGO – April 23, 2026 – iManage, the company dedicated to Making Knowledge Work™, today announced that Linda Henry has joined the company as Vice President of Customer Success, bringing extensive experience leading customer success organizations across SaaS businesses. In this role, Henry will lead iManage’s global Customer Success organization as the company continues to evolve as a multi-product SaaS platform and sharpen its focus on customer adoption, value realization, retention, and growth.

 

Henry joins iManage at a time of continued growth and product expansion. She will focus on helping the company build a more proactive, value-driven customer success model, with an emphasis on stronger cross-functional alignment, operational consistency, and the incorporation of AI capabilities into how the team supports customers. Her remit includes leading a global Customer Success organization of 50 team members, refining operating models and tiering strategies, and strengthening collaboration across Sales, Support, Marketing, Product, and the broader go-to-market organization.

 

“Linda brings the leadership experience, customer-first mindset, and operational discipline needed to help drive our next phase of growth,” said James Priz, Executive Vice President of Customer Experience at iManage. “She understands what it takes to build and scale modern customer success organizations, and her experience will be instrumental as we continue helping customers realize greater value from the iManage platform.”

 

Before joining iManage, Henry built her career across leading technology companies, including Salesforce, Google, AWS, and Microsoft, gaining deep experience in scaling customer-focused teams and supporting growth across complex global businesses. Her background aligns closely with iManage’s focus on evolving Customer Success into a more proactive, strategic function that strengthens adoption, retention, and long-term customer value.

 

“I joined iManage because it has the right combination of market leadership, growth opportunity, and commitment to innovation,” said Linda Henry, Vice President of Customer Success at iManage. “I’m excited to help evolve the customer success organization in ways that deepen customer value, strengthen long-term partnerships, and support the company’s next phase of growth.”

 

As Vice President of Customer Success, Henry will help further position Customer Success as a revenue-impacting organization at iManage, with a focus on scalable customer engagement, measurable adoption outcomes, and stronger alignment between customer value and long-term business growth.

 

Henry is based in Chicago and reports to James Priz.

 

About iManage

iManage is dedicated to Making Knowledge Work™. Our cloud-native platform is at the center of the knowledge economy, enabling every organization to work more productively, collaboratively, and securely. Built on more than 30 years of industry experience, iManage helps leading organizations manage documents and emails more efficiently, protect vital information assets, and leverage knowledge to drive better business outcomes. As your strategic business partner, we employ our award-winning AI-enabled technology, an extensive partner ecosystem, and a customer-centric approach to provide support and guidance you can trust to make knowledge work for you. iManage is relied on by more than one million professionals at 4,000 organizations around the world. Visit www.imanage.com to learn more.

news.titleEn: Microsoft releases new Legal Agent for Word
news.titleZh: 微软发布Word法律代理工具
news.summaryZh: 微软于4月30日宣布推出专为法律工作流设计的Legal Agent，该工具内置于Microsoft Word中，与法律工程师合作开发，支持合同审查和修订等任务。Legal Agent作为第一方体验，直接与Word的原生审阅工具（如修订和批注）集成，旨在支持Microsoft 365环境下的法律工作流。该代理能够实现基于剧本的合同分析、带有透明修订痕迹的谈判就绪修订，以及跨整个文档的可扩展起草。代理通过专用插入算法应用编辑，其修订引擎理解Word文档结构（包括格式、列表、表格和修订），并采用确定性解析层处理编辑，而非完全依赖大语言模型生成修订，从而提供更可靠的复杂合同处理基础，同时降低延迟和成本。这一进展引发关注，微软此前已在4月初为Copilot增加法律功能，与文档审查供应商形成竞争。微软凭借技术投资、用户熟悉度及安全合规的365环境具有优势，但法律工作流领域的成功仍需深度理解法律流程和产品卓越性。
news.bodyHtml:
It’s looked to be on the cards for a while and today (30 April), Microsoft announced its new Legal Agent, designed specifically for legal workflows in Microsoft Word. Developed in collaboration with legal engineers, Legal Agent is designed for workflows such as contract review and redlining, rather than adapting general-purpose AI to legal use cases.

As a first-party experience, Legal Agent works directly with Word’s native reviewing tools (including track changes and comments) and is designed to support legal workflows across Microsoft 365. Microsoft says that the agent enables playbook‑driven contract analysis, negotiation‑ready redlining with transparent track changes, and scalable drafting of precise, reviewable legal edits across entire documents.

Advertisement

A post from Microsoft Office Product Group president Sumit Chauhan today says: “The agent applies edits in the document through a purpose-built insertion algorithm to drive consistency regardless of how each edit was introduced. The agent’s redlining engine understands the structure of a Word document, not just visible text. It understands and structures Microsoft 365 document format into a representation that preserves formatting, lists, tables, and tracked changes. From there, the agent applies a deterministic resolution layer over the edits, including author-specific changes, instead of relying on an LLM to generate every revision directly. This provides a more reliable foundation for handling complex contracts while helping reduce latency and cost.”

This development will be watched with great and also wary interest. Microsoft has been increasingly building its legal specific capability, including earlier in April, new legal functionality in Copilot that put it in competition with document review vendors. On the one hand, its Microsoft, with its billions of tech investment, familiarity, and functionality that falls within the secure and governed 365 world. On the other, we know from experience that a deep understanding of the legal workflow and product excellence succeed over and above convenience every time in this space, so we await further information and updates.

news.titleEn: India’s legal tech market: Homegrown ambition and global inroads
news.titleZh: 印度法律科技市场：本土雄心与全球渗透
news.summaryZh:
印度正崛起为法律科技重要力量，数据显示该国拥有约1000家本土初创企业，数量仅次于美国。在RSGI举办的RISE Legal India会议上，与会者探讨了律所与法务部门如何应对贸易政策、技术变革与地缘政治不确定性。AI与数字化转型被列为优先事项，但印度律所仍在工具选择与核心基础设施建设上面临挑战。

印度法律市场存在本土平台与全球巨头之间的竞争。本土AI玩家如Lucio和Jurisphere已获得不同规模律所的采用，Trilegal（RSGI评定的印度前五律所之一）是Lucio的开发合作伙伴。全球平台也在渗透：Harvey被Shardul Amarchand Mangaldas、AZB & Partners等律所使用，Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas则采用了Legora。然而，购买AI许可并未完全转化为部署信心——在RISE Legal India的管理合伙人圆桌会议上，资深合伙人对AI错误带来的声誉风险表示深切担忧。

iManage的研究显示，印度法律从业者对AI潜力最为乐观，但平均每天仍花费37-40分钟查找信息，这被定义为“隐性搜索税”，本质是信息架构问题。在RSGI Resight 100榜单中的100家印度律所中，极少部署文档管理系统，但Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas自2009年起使用iManage，首席创新官Komal Gupta确认采用率达100%。印度法律市场对技术变革持开放态度，数字原生AI律所尚未出现，但势头已显。
news.bodyHtml:
By Mina Jenkins

India is emerging as a significant force in legal technology. Multiple data sources suggest the country is home to around 1,000 homegrown startups in the sector – second only to the United States. At RSGI’s RISE Legal India half-day conference in February, delegates examined how law firms and general counsel can navigate an era of disruptive trade policy, technological change and geopolitical uncertainty. AI and digital transformation ranked as clear priorities – yet, as in other legal markets, Indian law firms are wrestling with which tools to adopt as well as needing to make progress with their core infrastructure.

Advertisement

Homegrown or global tools?

One of the more interesting tensions in the Indian legal market is the pull between domestic platforms and global heavyweights. India has its own legal AI players — most notably Lucio and Jurisphere — which have found traction across firms of varying sizes and budgets. Notably, this is not simply a story of smaller firms choosing homegrown tools for cost reasons: Trilegal, rated by RSGI as one of India’s top five firms, was a development partner for Lucio.

Advertisement

Global platforms are nonetheless making serious inroads. Harvey is in use at Shardul Amarchand Mangaldas, AZB & Partners and S&A Law Offices, among others, while Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas has adopted Legora.

A willingness to purchase AI licences notably does not always translate into confidence about deployment: at RISE Legal India, during a managing partners roundtable attended by representatives of 15 leading firms, senior partners expressed deep concern about reputational exposure from AI errors – a concern that is only too familiar to legal market observers elsewhere.

The information architecture problem

Recent research from iManage, drawing on a survey of more than 3,200 decision-makers in professional services firms globally, includes a dedicated segment on the Indian legal market. It’s interesting to note that Indian practitioners rank among the most optimistic about AI’s potential: bullish on profitability and enthusiastic about what lies ahead. And yet the average Indian legal professional still loses between 37 and 40 minutes every day simply trying to find information. As iManage puts it, this is “the hidden search tax” — and critically, it is not an AI problem. It is an information architecture problem.

Of the 100 Indian law firms featured in the RSGI Resight 100, very few have document management systems in place. The exception is among the largest firms: Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas has used iManage since 2009, and chief innovation officer Komal Gupta confirmed that adoption within the firm is now at 100%. “Everything has to happen inside my iManage,” she noted — a discipline reinforced by deliberately limiting local hard drive storage on practitioners’ laptops.

What comes next

The Indian legal market clearly has an appetite for change. The openness to legal technology feels genuine rather than performative. A digital-native AI law firm has not yet emerged – though the general counsel of Premji Invest issued precisely that challenge to the room – but given the momentum, it seems a question of when rather than if.

news.titleEn: Legora raises $50m Series D extension – Atlassian and NVIDIA fund join as investors
news.titleZh: Legora 完成 5000 万美元 D 轮扩展融资，Atlassian 和 NVIDIA 旗下基金参投
news.summaryZh: Legora 于 4 月 30 日宣布完成 5000 万美元的 D 轮扩展融资，使该轮股权融资总额达到 6 亿美元，公司投后估值 56 亿美元。新投资者包括 Atlassian 和 NVIDIA 旗下风投部门 NVentures，以及 Adams Street Partners、Airtree、Barclays、Geodesic Capital、Insight Partners、Liberty Global 和 Nikesh Arora。Legora 近期年经常性收入突破 1 亿美元，员工数从 40 人增至 400 人，客户从 200 家扩展到 50 多个市场的 1000 多家组织，企业法务部门客户包括 Barclays，律所客户包括 White & Case、HSFK 和 Linklaters。企业 AI 正进入新阶段，基础模型快速进步，但真正的突破在于应用方式——AI 不仅辅助，还能在适当人类监督下自主执行。Legora 正在构建一个面向法律工作的全代理操作系统。
news.bodyHtml:
Legora today (30 April) announced a $50 million extension of its previously announced Series D financing, bringing the total round to $600 million in equity and valuing the company at $5.6 billion post-money. The extension adds Atlassian and NVentures (NVIDIA’s venture capital arm) as corporate investors, alongside new financial investors, including Adams Street Partners, Airtree, Barclays, Geodesic Capital, Insight Partners, Liberty Global and Nikesh Arora.

“As a leader in Legal AI, Legora is showing how deeply integrated, context-aware AI can transform complex workflows. We see strong alignment with Atlassian’s vision for AI-powered
team collaboration and look forward to supporting their continued expansion”, said Sarah Hughes, Atlassian’s head of corporate development and product partnerships.

Advertisement

The extended funding round follows a period of rapid growth. Legora recently surpassed $100 million in annual recurring revenue – placing it among the fastest-growing enterprise software
companies in history.

In terms of vital statistics, over the past year, Legora points out that it has scaled from 40 to 400 employees and expanded its customer base from 200 to more than 1,000 organizations across 50+ markets. Its corporate legal department clients include Barclays, and leading global firm clients include White & Case, HSFK, and Linklaters.

Advertisement

Corporate legal departments now represent one of Legora’s fastest-growing segments, and Legora’s founder and CEO, Max Junestrand, said: “Enterprise AI is now entering a new phase. Foundation models are improving rapidly, but the real breakthrough is in how they’re applied, where AI doesn’t just assist, but executes autonomously with the right level of human
oversight. With the support of our investors and customers, we’re building a full agentic operating system for legal work”.

news.titleEn: Slaughter and May goes firmwide with Harvey
news.titleZh: 司力达律师事务所全所推广Harvey AI平台
news.summaryZh: 司力达律师事务所（Slaughter and May）将在全所范围内推广Harvey的AI平台，成为最新一家选择企业级法律AI工具的顶级律所。该所表示将在所有业务领域采用Harvey的全平台，支持律师处理跨境并购、尽职调查、监管研究和文件分析等事务。采用Harvey旨在提升客户服务，关键在于对人员的投资，作为监督AI的关键人力层。AI能连接并应用律所的深厚经验，增强集体判断力、创造力和问题解决能力。Harvey因其代理能力、安全性、在大型律所中领导AI转型的经验、客户基础覆盖以及满足律所严格标准的能力而被选中。Harvey的转型办公室将与律所合作，确保AI负责任且有效地部署。
news.bodyHtml:
Slaughter and May is rolling out Harvey’s AI platform firm wide, becoming the latest major law firm to select an enterprise legal AI tool – although two of its magic circle peers have so far forged their own path instead.

Slaughter and May says it is adopting Harvey’s full platform across all practice areas to support its lawyers on multi-jurisdictional matters spanning M&A, due diligence, regulatory research, and document analysis. 

Advertisement

David Johnson, Slaughter and May’s managing partner, said: “Adopting Harvey firmwide allows us to enhance the excellent service that we provide to our clients. Critical to our adoption is the investment we make in our people, as the vital human layer that supervises AI.” 

Sally Wokes, a partner and head of Slaughter and May’s Innovation Committee, added: “Our differentiator is the depth and quality of our experience. AI allows us to connect and apply that expertise in different situations, enhancing the collective judgement, creativity and problem solving we bring to client matters.” 

Advertisement

A statement sent out after work hours UK-time yesterday (29 April) said that Harvey was selected for its agentic capabilities and security, its proven experience leading AI transformation inside major law firms, its presence across the firm’s client base, and its ability to meet the firm’s exacting standards. Harvey’s Transformation Office, which includes seasoned legal experts, will work alongside the firm to support the rollout and ensure AI is adopted responsibly and effectively across the business. 

Winston Weinberg, CEO of Harvey, said in the press release: “Slaughter and May has built its reputation for excellence over 130 years by pairing deep legal expertise and outstanding lawyers with a willingness to embrace new technologies. We are honoured to support the firm and its clients as they apply AI to some of the most consequential legal work in the world.” 

A&O Shearman was the first law firm to select Harvey and fellow magic circle law firm Linklaters has largely gone with Legora. Clifford Chance and Freshfields have selected neither to date, with Clifford Chance doubling down on Microsoft Copilot and its Assist AI tool, and Freshfields striking a firmwide agreement with Anthropic.

news.titleEn: Agentic Systems Add New Layer of AI Hallucination Risk in Legal Work
news.titleZh: 代理系统为法律工作增添新一层AI幻觉风险
news.summaryZh: 随着新一代代理工具迅速进入市场，律师和支持人员需要防范更多类型的潜在错误。代理AI工具可能放大生成式AI中出现的幻觉，使未加检查的错误在多步骤工作流程中累积。此外，代理工具还呈现新型幻觉，错误不仅出现在工具生成的信息中，还出现在工具完成任务的过程中。这些新错误部分源于代理工具的构建和运行方式：AI代理可以创建或与其他代理交互，分配用户请求的各个部分，从而在代理与人类以及代理之间的通信中产生幻觉。例如，主代理可能声称已向特定代理发出指令，但实际上并未执行；子代理可能报告已研究法律数据库并返回结果，但实际上并未进行查询，而是基于训练数据产生了幻觉。代理利用工具与其他程序交互的能力也带来风险。代理通过工具调用执行操作，若参数错误，所需操作可能失败，且子代理可能不向主代理或用户报告失败结果。除非严格限制代理可访问的工具和可执行的操作，否则它们可能选择错误工具或危及敏感数据。代理工具在效率与安全之间存在权衡，尤其在法律等受监管行业，处理敏感信息需要更高谨慎。负责任部署代理工具需要持续人工监督，工作流程中应设置控制点以便干预、验证和纠正。Popov Ledinski补充，法律团队倾向于采用定义明确的代理工作流程，而非完全自主的系统，大型律所主要在沙盒和实验环境中进行探索。
news.bodyHtml:
With a new generation of agentic tools rapidly entering the market, lawyers and support staff will also need to guard against even more kinds of potential misfires.

Agentic AI tools can magnify the kinds of hallucinations that can appear with gen AI tools, enabling unchecked errors to compound over the course of a multistep workflow.

But agentic tools also present novel forms of hallucinations, with errors appearing not just in the information a tool produces, but also in the very process the tool uses to complete a task.

Rok Popov Ledinski, founder and CEO of MPL Legal Tech Advisors, told Law.com that these new kinds of potential errors derive in part from the way agentic tools are built and how they operate. AI agents can create or interact with other agents that they task with various components of a user’s request, creating opportunities for hallucinations in both agent-to-human and agent-to-agent communications.

“Maybe the main agent that you're communicating with will say that it has given instructions to a specific agent, but in fact, it hasn't. It has hallucinated that to you,” he said.

“A sub-agent that was given a task to go and research a specific legal database will come back to the main agent saying, ... ‘Hey, I researched the legal database, here's the result of what I have found.’ That by itself might be a hallucination, because it never went and researched the legal database, it hallucinated the things based on its training data,” he added.

The ability of agents to leverage tools and interact with other programs presents another source of possible danger. One of the major advantages of agentic systems is their ability to use other software platforms, performing tasks previous gen AI tools could not on their own, like accessing data from document management systems (DMS).

To do so, agents perform an action called a tool call, where they may provide a sub-agent with parameters for how to use another piece of software. However, if these parameters are incorrect, the required action with the other tool may fail, and the sub-agent may not report that outcome to the main agent or to the user.

“Before gen AI, you would click a button, and that button meant that some information was pulled from your [DMS]—that was 100% successful all the time,” Popov Ledinski said. “Now you have this small AI that is sitting in between those two systems, and here there's [a higher percentage of] failures than we have seen before.”

Unless agents are strictly limited in what tools they can access and what actions they can perform, they can also pick the wrong tools or compromise or valuable data.

“There's no necessary governing mechanism over what it's doing,” said Tom Barnett, senior director at legal innovation and technology advisory firm Maker5 and former chief data officer at Jackson Lewis. “It has the potential to go out into the world and start doing what you told it to do, but maybe you didn't think of all the consequences of what you asked, or there's some other bug in what it's doing.”

Necessary Caution

Agentic tools can present organizations with a steep tradeoff between efficiency and safety. The ability to act autonomously is part of what allows AI agents to help users perform tasks more quickly, but that autonomy can be the source of damaging mistakes, especially if the system is not set up to allow users to trace and monitor the steps it takes.

This tradeoff is particularly stark in law and other regulated industries that deal with sensitive or confidential information, mandating an elevated level of caution, particularly since structuring and evaluating technology safeguards lies outside the core functions of law firms.

“[Law firms] are really great at delivering legal services, but they're not at their core technical organizations, so I don't know that they're in a great position to be at the cutting edge of implementing technology, using it, governing it,” Barnett said.

While agentic tools will likely continue to improve, this won’t eliminate the potential for hallucinations and similar errors. The underlying large language models that power agentic tools are generally rewarded for their output while being trained, which can make them less likely to tell a user they could not perform a requested action. Popov Ledinski also noted that some researchers have found that hallucination rates can actually increase as models develop more sophisticated reasoning capabilities.

Will Gaus, chief knowledge management and innovation officer at Troutman Pepper Locke, told Law.com that responsible deployment of agentic tools in a legal setting requires continued human oversight of the work done by agents.

“Control points should be built into workflows so there is the ability to intervene, validate and correct when needed,” he noted. “The firms that get this right treat agentic AI as a controlled extension of their existing processes, not as an autonomous layer operating alongside them.”

Popov Ledinski added that the need to move cautiously has led legal teams to introduce defined agentic workflows rather than embracing fully autonomous systems like OpenClaw, a popular AI agent that can present dangerous vulnerabilities.

“There are a lot of agentic use cases today in law firms. However, when you when you think of the more autonomous ones, where the agent comes up with what is the next step to complete the task that I have been given, I do not see real life deployments,” he said. “I see Big Law firms experimenting with that, the ones that have invested in sandboxes and experimentational environments before.”

news.titleEn: Supreme Court Opens Federal Door for Oil Companies in Louisiana Coastal Suits
news.titleZh: 最高法院为石油公司在路易斯安那州沿海诉讼中打开联邦法院大门
news.summaryZh: 美国最高法院一致裁定，石油和天然气公司可在路易斯安那州沿海损害诉讼中依据联邦官员移送条款将案件移送联邦法院，前提是涉案行为与战时为联邦政府生产燃料相关。该裁决未涉及环境索赔的实质问题，但可能显著改变诉讼地点和方式。路易斯安那州诉讼是更广泛的“遗留责任”纠纷的一部分，涉及数十年油气活动导致的沿海土地流失和环境损害。原告通常偏好州法院，而被告则争取联邦管辖权。最高法院的裁决加强了被告援引28 U.S.C. § 1442条款的能力，主张部分生产活动是在国家战时需求期间根据联邦指示进行的。联邦官员移送已成为涉及政府合同、联邦指导运营和受监管行业案件中企业被告日益重要的管辖权工具。联邦法院可能影响动议实践、上诉选项、多地区诉讼协调、专家证据可采性及整体诉讼杠杆。对于面临大规模侵权、环境或公共实体索赔的公司，该意见提醒应尽早评估并谨慎保留与政府监管相关的移送论点。对诉讼律师而言，实际意义立竿见影：预计将出现关于移送、发回重审以及证明原告指控与联邦指示之间存在充分联系的事实记录的新一轮争论。法院的推理也可能影响其他具有战时或政府承包商历史的行业。对于内部法律顾问和合规团队，该裁决强调了历史记录的价值。合同、生产指令、与联邦机构的通信以及档案运营材料可能成为实体抗辩和法院策略的核心。该裁决还凸显了程序性裁决对重大诉讼下游影响的系统性重要性。环境索赔仍然存在，但法院战场的转移可能产生超越路易斯安那州海岸的广泛影响。
news.relevanceReason: 文章主要讨论最高法院关于联邦法院管辖权的程序性裁决，涉及石油公司环境诉讼，但未聚焦法律AI或法律技术，仅与法律程序相关。

news.titleEn: LexisNexis Owner RELX Announces Plans to Acquire Legal Tech Company Doctrine
news.titleZh: LexisNexis母公司RELX宣布计划收购法律科技公司Doctrine
news.summaryZh: RELX计划收购法律科技公司Doctrine，交易条款未披露。RELX表示将利用Doctrine的法律搜索、分析和起草工作流程，增强其在欧洲的法律技术产品和服务。欢迎Doctrine加入，以更好地服务法国、欧洲及其他地区的客户。Doctrine成立于2016年，为法律专业人士提供法律研究和情报软件，其平台使用生成式人工智能分析法院判决并提供洞察和数据解决方案。收购完成后，两家公司在过渡期间将继续独立运营。此次收购公告发布前，RELX的风险投资部门REV于1月参与了房地产法律工作AI平台Orbital的B轮融资。
news.bodyHtml:
Terms of the transaction were not disclosed.

RELX plans to leverage Doctrine’s legal search, analysis and drafting workflows to bolster its current legal technology offerings and presence in Europe, according to a press release.

“We are excited about the prospect of welcoming Doctrine, so that we can serve customers in France, across Europe, and beyond in even greater ways,” said Sean Fitzpatrick, CEO of LexisNexis North America, UK and Ireland, in the release. “Doctrine’s customer-centric innovation approach, powerful platform and expert talent complement LexisNexis’s global capabilities in authoritative legal AI workflow solutions, and we look forward to delivering even more value to customers."

Founded in 2016 by Nicolas Bustamante, Antoine Dusséaux and Raphaël Champeimont, Doctrine provides legal research and intelligence software for legal professionals, and its platform uses generative artificial intelligence to analyze court decisions and provide insights and data analytics solutions and drafting.

When it comes to whether RELX intends to integrate Doctrine and LexisNexis offerings, LexisNexis told Law.com in a statement that "the proposed acquisition is subject to the completion of applicable information and consultation procedures with the relevant employee representative bodies and customary regulatory consents. The two companies will continue to operate separately in the interim."

The acquisition offer announcement comes several months after RELX’s venture capital arm REV participated in a Series B funding round for Orbital, a London and New York-based AI-powered platform for real estate legal work, in January.

news.titleEn: Legora Raises $50M Series D Extension, With Backing From Nvidia Fund
news.titleZh: Legora获5000万美元D轮扩展融资，英伟达基金参投
news.summaryZh: Legora宣布获得5000万美元D轮扩展融资，由软件公司Atlassian和AI芯片开发商英伟达的风险投资部门NVentures领投，Barclays、Insight Partners、Adams Street Partners、Airtree、Geodesic Capital、Liberty Global及Nikesh Arora参投。此轮融资建立在Legora于3月完成的5.5亿美元D轮融资（由Accel领投）基础之上。资金将用于加速Legora业务及代理操作系统的增长。基础模型快速进步，真正的突破在于应用方式，AI不仅辅助，还能在适当人类监督下自主执行。公司正在为法律工作构建完整的代理操作系统。此次融资约在Legora宣布收购斯德哥尔摩研究初创公司Qura一周后完成，Qura主要利用大语言模型构建和导航法律数据库。NVentures是首次涉足法律科技领域，而Insight Partners此前已投资Filevine、Flank、LawVu、Litera等法律科技公司。Barclays的投资则是在Legora技术被该银行内部法律团队采用一个月后做出。
news.bodyHtml:
The additional funding was led by software company Atlassian as well as NVentures, the venture capital arm of AI chip developer Nvidia. Participation also included Barclays, Insight Partners, Adams Street Partners, Airtree, Geodesic Capital, Liberty Global and Nikesh Arora.

The capital builds on Legora’s initial $550 million Series D funding round, announced in March and led by Accel.

The extension will bolster rapid growth of Legora’s business and agentic operating system, according to a press release.

“Foundation models are improving rapidly, but the real breakthrough is in how they’re applied, where AI doesn’t just assist, but executes autonomously with the right level of human oversight,” Legora co-founder and CEO Max Junestrand said in the release. “With the support of our investors and customers, we’re building a full agentic operating system for legal work”

This funding extension comes roughly a week after Legora announced its acquisition of Qura, a Stockholm-based research startup that assembles legal databases largely built using and navigated by large language models (LLMs).

The extension’s contributors are made up of investors who are both familiar and new to the legal tech industry.

NVentures’ investment is the firm’s first foray into legal technology, according to its available portfolio on its website. The firm acts as a venture arm to Nvidia, which develops chips for computer graphics and AI data centers.

On the other hand, Insight Partners’ contribution to Legora’s funding round extension is one of many investments the global venture capital and private equity firm has made in the legal tech industry. The New York-based firm has previously invested in Filevine, Flank, LawVu, Litera, among others.

Barclays’ investment comes a month after Legora announced that its technology has been rolled out with the bank’s in-house legal team.

news.titleEn: DOJ Challenges New Jersey Law Limiting Federal Officers
news.titleZh: 美国司法部挑战新泽西州限制联邦官员的法律
news.summaryZh: 美国司法部对新泽西州、州长米基·谢里尔和总检察长詹妮弗·达文波特提起诉讼，指控该州的《执法人员保护法》非法限制联邦执法活动。该案在新泽西联邦法院提起，直接触及联邦官员在州境内行动时州权力的界限。争议核心是宪法层面的问题：州是否有权监管、限制或对执行联邦职责的联邦官员施加条件。联邦政府预计将主张新泽西州法律因干涉核心联邦执法职能而被联邦法律优先适用，并违反最高条款。新泽西州则可能将该法辩护为州警察权的合法行使，旨在保护居民并为州内活动制定规则。
news.relevanceReason: 文章主要讨论联邦与州在执法权力上的宪法冲突，属于联邦制和法律优先适用问题，虽涉及法律领域，但核心并非法律AI或法律科技，而是政府权力和宪法诉讼。

news.titleEn: Microsoft Launches Legal Agent in Word
news.titleZh: 微软在Word中推出法律代理工具
news.summaryZh: 其新推出的法律代理工具可分析文档、起草修改意见并检查合同是否符合用户组织的内部标准。该工具允许用户跟踪更改并查看代理的编辑及其建议所依据的引用。目前，该法律代理工具仅在美国向参与微软早期访问计划Frontier的Windows桌面版Word用户开放。博客文章未说明该工具的全面发布时间。该代理的修订引擎能够理解Word文档的结构，包括格式、列表、表格和修订标记，并通过确定性解析层处理编辑，而非完全依赖大语言模型生成每次修订，从而为处理复杂合同提供更可靠的基础，同时有助于降低延迟和成本。该法律代理工具的推出距离微软宣布Word、Excel和PowerPoint中新的代理AI功能全面可用约一周时间。微软此前已提供法律相关工具，例如其数据治理与安全平台Microsoft Purview中的电子发现工具。微软此举标志着主流科技公司进一步进军法律领域。今年早些时候，Anthropic在Claude的代理AI产品Cowork中推出法律插件，引发法律科技市场关注。
news.bodyHtml:
The new Legal Agent is designed to analyze documents, draft edits and check contracts for compliance with the user organization’s internal standards, according to a blog post from Microsoft. The tool allows users to track changes and review the agent's edits and citations supporting its suggestions.

The Legal Agent is currently available on Word on Windows desktop to participants in Microsoft’s early-access Frontier program in the U.S. The blog post did not state when the agent will be broadly released.

“The agent’s redlining engine understands the structure of a Word document, not just visible text. It understands and structures Microsoft 365 document format into a representation that preserves formatting, lists, tables and tracked changes. From there, the agent applies a deterministic resolution layer over the edits, including author-specific changes, instead of relying on an LLM to generate every revision directly,” the company said in its blog post. “This provides a more reliable foundation for handling complex contracts while helping reduce latency and cost.”

The introduction of the Legal Agent comes about a week after Microsoft announced the general availability of new agentic AI capabilities in Word, Excel and PowerPoint.

The agent is not the first offering Microsoft has created for law-related tasks. The company—whose products are widely used in the legal industry—also offers an e-discovery tool within Microsoft Purview, its data governance and security platform.

Microsoft’s introduction of its Legal Agent marks a further encroachment of mainstream tech companies into the legal space.

Earlier this year, Anthropic caused a stir in the legal tech market with the introduction of a legal plugin within Claude's agentic AI Cowork offering. While some saw the plugin as a potential threat to certain legal-specific tech companies, others predicted that the tool would ultimately prove an asset to the legal tech industry.

news.titleEn: The Hidden Cost of Agentic AI: Information Governance
news.titleZh: 代理型AI的隐性成本：信息治理
news.summaryZh: 法律行业正从生成式AI向代理型AI过渡，后者不仅能响应提示，还能推理、规划并执行多步骤任务。Womble Bond Dickinson律所测试了代理型AI在监管监控和复杂诉讼中的应用：代理可自动监测立法更新、筛选相关信息、检索数据并生成备忘录，或根据战略目标分析证人证词与内部通信的矛盾，构建时间线并起草交叉询问脚本。然而，代理型AI的可靠性取决于底层数据质量，而律所普遍存在数据分类不清、元数据稀疏、特权标识缺失等问题。该律所已将代理型AI设计团队与信息治理部门整合，强调在部署代理前必须明确数据分类、访问权限、保留策略和伦理墙。代理型AI的真正挑战不在于提示工程，而在于清理过去十年松散治理的内容。未来，律师的角色将转向法律架构师和代理监督者，专注于设定战略参数、审计推理链并确保保密义务。信息治理被视为代理型AI的入场成本，而非事后考虑。
news.bodyHtml:
Today, that tool is no longer reactive. It is moving into the passenger seat, acting as a copilot, reading the road ahead.

The industry is moving through a predictable adoption curve. Rules-based search and document management gave way to generative AI, which introduced conversational tools that draft, summarize and synthesize at a level that surprised even early adopters. The next shift is already underway: agentic AI, systems that do not just respond to prompts but reason, plan and execute across multiple steps. This is the move from tools you use to partners that act. It also carries a cost most firms have not priced in, and that cost is information governance.

From Conversation to Action

If generative AI is like a consultant you talk to, agentic AI is more like an associate you can delegate to. You set a goal, and it figures out how to achieve it.

At Womble Bond Dickinson, our team has been testing this distinction in practice. Consider regulatory monitoring. A client operating across dozens of jurisdictions faces a real information problem. Traditionally, paralegals manually scan legislative updates. An agentic approach reframes the problem. The agent monitors activity continuously, filters for relevance against the client’s footprint and acts when something material occurs. When a new carbon tax passes, the agent identifies the affected subsidiary, retrieves emissions data from a secure firm repository and produces a privileged memorandum for partner review. A self-initiated model with an attorney always in the loop.

A second example is complex litigation. Rather than asking an AI to find emails about a specific meeting, the lawyer assigns a strategic goal: identify inconsistencies between a witness’s deposition and their internal communications on a merger valuation. The agent builds a timeline, cross-references figures, flags logical gaps and drafts a suggested cross-examination script with hyperlinked evidence. It is not just retrieving information but executing a strategy.

Governance Is the Entry Fee

Vendor demos rarely mention it, but an agent is only as trustworthy as the data it touches. When a system acts autonomously across repositories, every poorly tagged document, every orphaned matter folder and every undocumented retention rule becomes a liability.

At our firm, we formalized integration between our agentic AI design team and the information governance unit, not just an innovation unit, for exactly this reason. Before an agent operates on a matter file, someone has to answer basic questions. What is the data classification? Who can see it? What is the retention posture? Which ethical walls apply? Most firms have not answered these questions at the level of granularity an agent requires. The real work of agentic AI is not prompt engineering. It is the unglamorous work of cleaning up a decade of loosely governed content.

The Data Problem

This exposes a broader issue. Law firms have a data problem that is undermining their AI initiatives. Firm knowledge lives in matter management systems, document management systems, email archives, time entry records, and practice databases that were never designed to talk to one another. Fields are inconsistent. Taxonomy drifts across practice groups. Metadata is sparse. Privilege designations are often implicit rather than tagged.

Generative AI hides this problem because it works off the prompt in front of it. Agentic AI exposes it. An agent that is supposed to pull precedent, check conflicts and draft a closing memo cannot do so if the underlying data is unreliable. The firms seeing real return on AI investment are the ones spending on data quality, taxonomy and integration before scaling agents.

World Models Will Challenge the Current Approach

There is a longer horizon worth watching. Today’s AI agents reason through language. They read context, plan and act on text-based representations of the world. World models represent something different. They build internal simulations of systems and environments and reason by running them forward. Applied to legal work, a world model could simulate the likely trajectory of a regulatory regime, the downstream effects of a contract clause under different enforcement scenarios or how a litigation strategy plays out across multiple judges and jurisdictions.

This approach will challenge today’s agentic architectures. Text-native agents will need to interface with simulation-native systems. Governance and data questions will become harder, not easier. Firms still catching up to language models should pay attention to what comes next.

The Changing Role of the Lawyer

Agentic AI also reshapes the profession itself. Junior associates traditionally built foundational skills through the intensive document work that agents now handle. That training pathway is now being disrupted. The lawyer of the near future will function more as a legal architect and agent supervisor. The work will focus on setting strategic parameters, auditing reasoning chains, and ensuring everything stays within the bounds of client confidentiality and professional responsibility. Firms will need to be thoughtful about how they develop legal intuition in a generation that may never perform the foundational tasks their predecessors did.

The Path Forward

The tipping point is not about whether agentic AI will arrive. It has arrived. The advantage will go to firms that treat information governance as the real cost of admission, not an afterthought. The attorney of the future is less a solo practitioner and more an orchestrator of capabilities, deploying a research agent, a drafting agent, and a compliance monitor, then coordinating their outputs into a unified strategy. The skills that matter are knowing which agent to deploy, interrogating its reasoning, and applying the judgment only a human lawyer can provide.

Chad Ergun is the chief information officer at Womble Bond Dickinson, where he leads technology strategy, innovation, and AI transformation. His work spans generative AI, knowledge management, cybersecurity, eDiscovery, machine learning, and data science, with an emphasis on applying emerging technologies to modernize legal service delivery.

news.titleEn: ILTA EVOLVE: Sometimes Less Is More — A Focus On Leadership
news.titleZh: ILTA EVOLVE：有时少即是多——聚焦领导力
news.summaryZh: ILTA Evolve会议于4月30日在丹佛开幕，这是作者连续第三年参加。会议规模小、聚焦，能过滤大型法律科技会议的噪音。今年新增第三大支柱：法律科技领导力。鉴于律所正面临生成式AI颠覆、网络安全风险升级以及以更少资源做更多事的压力，这一主题恰逢其时。会议将有两场主题演讲、20多场分会和三个专题讨论，以及ILTA著名的Klickers活动。
news.bodyText:
ILTA EVOLVE: Sometimes Less Is More — A Focus On Leadership

By Stephen Embry on April 30, 2026

Posted in Uncategorized

Here’s my preview of ILTA’s Evolve conference that starts today in Denver for Above the Law. This is the thrid year in a row I have attended. I keep coming back for the same reasons: it’s small, focused, and cuts through the noise that dominates many large legal tech conferences.

This year ILTA has added a third pillar to the conference’s program: Leadership in Legal Tech. With all that law firms are trying to navigate right now, GenAI disruption, escalating cybersecurity risks, and pressure to do more with less, that addition seems pretty timely.

Looking forward to two strong keynotes, over 20 sessions, and three focused topics. And the Klickers for which ILTA is famous.

news.titleEn: The Common Plumbing: Andrea Orcel’s Bull Case for a Convergent Europe
news.titleZh: 共同管道：Andrea Orcel看多欧洲一体化的理由
news.summaryZh: 在Semafor世界经济峰会上，UniCredit首席执行官Andrea Orcel提出，欧洲需构建统一的数字与金融操作系统，以与美国大型银行竞争。欧洲过去二十年表现低于潜力，根源在于缺乏一体化，而非人才或资源不足。Orcel以收购德国商业银行的案例说明，欧洲跨境交易虽需应对多国政治，但能形成更稳健的均衡。UniCredit目前实现20%有形股本回报率和38%成本收入比，证明泛欧模式在碎片化环境中可行。欧洲缺乏成熟的资本市场，导致储蓄流向美国，形成“燃料短缺”。他呼吁推进资本市场联盟，使欧洲企业获得本土融资。此外，欧洲面临人才外流，许多诺贝尔奖得主在欧洲出生却在美国获奖。未来5至10年将决定欧洲是沦为“工业革命的波兰”还是成为全球领导者。
news.bodyText:
At the Semafor World Economy summit, held during the high-level World Bank and IMF Spring Meetings, the “Future of Global Finance” took a decidedly Continental turn. While the morning headlines focused on U.S. inflation and Middle Eastern volatility, Andrea Orcel , CEO of UniCredit SpA , sat down with Thorold Barker to address the “Sandwich Question”: Does anybody still care about Europe?

From a technologist’s vantage point, Orcel’s argument was less about banking and more about systems architecture . He framed Europe not as a failing experiment, but as a powerful engine running on “fragmented plumbing.” For Europe to compete with the sheer scale of U.S. “hyperscale” banks like JPMorgan, it must stop optimizing for individual nations and start building a common digital and financial operating system.

The Macro View: The Convergence Imperative

Orcel was refreshingly blunt: Europe has been “punching below its weight” for two decades. The macro-economic gap between the U.S. and Europe isn’t just a matter of culture; it’s a matter of market capitalization and scale . Today, JPMorgan and Bank of America are worth roughly the same as the top ten European banks combined.

Orcel argues that this isn’t due to a lack of talent or resources, but a lack of convergence . While the U.S. operates on a unified “platform” of trade, law, and regulation, Europe remains a patchwork of barriers. To survive the “Cognitive Industrial Revolution,” Orcel believes Europe must move beyond being a collection of sovereign silos and toward a Common Denominator approach in energy, defense, and finance.

The Micro View: Patience and the Commerzbank “Steak”

On a granular, operational level, Orcel provided a masterclass in the “Long Game” of European M&A. His ongoing pursuit of Germany’s Commerzbank serves as a perfect micro-case for the friction inherent in the European system.

The Stakeholder Equilibrium:

The “Steak” Strategy: Orcel described the process of building a stake in Commerzbank as a patient, transparent attempt to explain value to a wide array of stakeholders, shareholders, employees, and clients.

The Decision Loop: Unlike the U.S., where a CEO can “go right down to the middle and take the decision,” Europe requires navigating a web of national governments and cross-border politics. Orcel argued that while this makes the loop longer, it creates a more resilient “equilibrium” once the deal is struck.

The Success Metric: He noted that UniCredit’s current success, boasting a 20% Return on Tangible Equity (RoTE) and a 38% cost-to-income ratio, is the tangible proof that a leaner, pan-European approach works even within a fragmented environment.

Notable Insights from Andrea Orcel

“Europe has been consistently punching below its weight… we have been talking about not crystallizing on the opportunity of a united Europe. The time is now.”

“If you want to transform, that is the machine. The bank is the machine, the capital market is the gasoline. In one, we are undersized; in the other, we are under-present. Together, Europe does not have the fuel to do what it needs to do.”

“People are less and less ready to accept stories that demonize Europe in favor of non-convergence.”

The Fuel Problem: Banking vs. Capital Markets

For the technologists in the room, Orcel’s most “clever” analogy involved the Fuel of Transformation . He argued that Europe’s lack of sophisticated capital markets acts as a “gasoline shortage” for the “banking machine.”

Currently, European savings are largely funneled into U.S.-based institutional investors, who then direct that capital back into U.S. or Chinese markets. Europe is essentially exporting its “fuel” (savings) to power other people’s transformations. To reverse this, Europe needs a Capital Markets Union (CMU) that allows European companies to be funded by European investors, keeping the innovation cycle, and the wealth, within the continent.

The Talent Leak: Nobel Prizes and Mobility

Orcel pointed to a poignant micro-stat: many Nobel Prize winners are European-born but won their awards while working in the U.S. This is the ultimate “brain drain” metric. Europe has the talent pool and the education, but it lacks the convergent infrastructure that allows that talent to “fire” at a global scale. He believes that by closing the mismatch between “haves and have-nots” through convergence, Europe can create value opportunities that keep its best minds at home.

Final Takeaway

Andrea Orcel’s view is that Europe is at a “jump” point. The next 5 to 10 years will determine whether it becomes a “Poland of the Industrial Revolution” or a global leader. His “European Optimism” is built on the fact that the downside of staying fragmented is now so apparent that the “wake-up call” has finally been heard by the national governments.

For the global technologist, the message is clear: watch the plumbing. If Europe can fix its common denominator, it remains one of the largest untapped value-creation opportunities in the world.

news.titleEn: Supreme Court Invalidates Louisiana’s SB8 Map in Major Racial Gerrymandering Ruling
news.titleZh: 最高法院裁定路易斯安那州SB8选区地图违宪，重大种族不公划分案落槌
news.summaryZh: 4月29日，美国最高法院裁定路易斯安那州的国会选区地图违宪，认定该州SB8计划构成种族不公划分。法院认为《投票权法》并未要求路易斯安那州增设一个多数少数族裔选区，因此该州不能以遵守联邦投票权法作为种族划线依据。该判决立即重塑了选区划分争议的法律格局。核心问题在于该州重划选区时是否以种族为主要因素，以及能否通过严格审查。法院驳回了州政府以《投票权法》为必要性的辩护，指出联邦法律并未强制要求SB8中的额外多数少数族裔选区。州政府若以种族为主要因素划分选区，必须证明其地图是为实现重大利益而量身定制，且需有充分法律依据，而非泛泛的担忧或诉讼风险。对于诉讼律师而言，该意见将成为挑战选区地图的核心依据，各方将围绕是否实际需要增设少数族裔机会选区、种族或政治因素是否主导划线过程展开激烈证据争夺。判决对正在进行的补救地图争议、紧急申请及选举日程诉讼具有实际意义。对于法务、政府事务及合规专业人士，判决提醒种族意识决策即使以联邦合规为名，仍受严格司法审查。该判决将影响全美各州如何记录选区划分选择、评估《投票权法》第2条风险及在法庭上辩护地图。简言之，法院表明各州不能将《投票权法》视为种族划区的全面安全港，这一信号将影响下一波选举争议中的选区划分策略。
news.relevanceReason: 文章主要讨论美国最高法院关于种族不公划分的选举法裁决，涉及《投票权法》和选区重划，但未聚焦法律AI或法律科技，仅对选举法律从业者有间接关联。

news.titleEn: Actionstep Honored as Bronze Stevie® Award Winner in 2026 American Business Awards®
news.titleZh: Actionstep 荣获 2026 年美国商业奖® 史蒂夫® 铜奖
news.summaryZh: 法律会计与律所管理软件提供商 Actionstep 凭借其 AI 助手 Scout 获得第 24 届美国商业奖® 客户服务技术最佳应用类别史蒂夫® 铜奖。Scout 于 2025 年 4 月上线，经过一年开发测试，旨在提供 7×24 小时自助支持，减轻人工客服负担。上线以来，Scout 既能解决常见支持问题，也能通过分步指导协助用户处理复杂的法律会计与律所管理工作流。此外，Scout 还成为内部工具，用于新员工入职培训。该计划正扩展至整个 Actionstep 集团。本届美国商业奖共收到超过 3700 份提名，涵盖初创公司、高管、最佳新产品等多个类别。全球 230 多位专业人士参与评审。颁奖典礼将于 6 月 9 日在纽约举行。
news.bodyHtml:
Actionstep was named the winner of a Bronze Stevie® Award in the Best Use of Technology in Customer Service category in The 24th Annual American Business Awards® today, recognizing the company’s AI assistant, Scout. 

The American Business Awards are the United States’ premier business awards program. All organizations operating in the US are eligible to submit nominations. 

More than 3,700 nominations from individuals and organizations of all sizes and in virtually every industry were submitted this year for consideration in a wide range of categories, including Startup of the Year, Executive of the Year, Best New Product or Service of the Year, Marketing Campaign of the Year, Thought Leader of the Year, and App of the Year, among others. Actionstep was nominated in the Best Use of Technology in Customer Service category for its work as a legal accounting and practice management software provider. 

Scout is Actionstep’s AI assistant, built with robust adaptability and exceptional learning capabilities. Launched in April 2025 following a year of meticulous development and testing, Scout was designed to provide 24/7 self-service support for Actionstep customers, reducing the burden on human support agents while delivering fast, accurate assistance. Since its launch, Scout has proven equally capable of resolving common support issues and guiding customers through complex legal accounting and practice management workflows with thorough, step-by-step instructions. Beyond customer support, Scout has also become a valuable internal tool, helping to onboard and train new employees by drawing on Actionstep’s entire knowledge base. The initiative is now expanding across the broader Actionstep group, demonstrating its scalable value as the company continues to grow. 

“This award reflects our commitment to pairing technology with genuine customer empathy. Scout wasn’t built to replace the human touch. It was built to extend it, giving our customers faster answers and our team the space to focus on the moments that truly matter. Being recognized by the American Business Awards validates that approach, and motivates us to keep pushing the boundaries of what great customer service looks like.” — Daniella Bohill, SVP of Customer Success, Actionstep 

More than 230 professionals worldwide participated in the judging process to select this year’s Stevie Award winners. 

“Organizations across the United States continue to set a high standard for innovation and performance,” said Stevie Awards president Maggie Miller. “The breadth and quality of nominations submitted to The 2026 American Business Awards reflect a dynamic and competitive business environment, where organizations are finding new ways to drive growth, deliver value, and make an impact. We congratulate all of this year’s Stevie Award winners and look forward to celebrating their accomplishments at our June 9 awards ceremony in New York.” 

Details about The American Business Awards and the list of 2026 Stevie winners are available at https://ABA.StevieAwards.com.

news.titleEn: China’s Meta-Manus block adds new risk layer to cross-border AI diligence
news.titleZh: 中国叫停Meta-Manus交易，为跨境AI尽职调查增添新风险维度
news.summaryZh:
4月27日，中国国家发展和改革委员会责令Meta Platforms与AI初创公司Manus解除一项约20亿美元的收购交易，该交易于四个月前完成。这是自2021年中国外资安全审查框架生效以来，首次公开宣布的AI领域外商投资禁令。NDRC要求双方终止整合运营并撤销交易。截至4月30日，两家公司均未公布退出计划或上诉策略。Meta发言人表示交易“完全符合适用法律”，并预期“调查将得到适当解决”。

该决定对从事电子取证、信息治理和网络安全的律师及采购负责人具有实际影响。涉及中国来源工程、训练数据依赖或离岸重组公司历史的供应商，现在面临NDRC和CFIUS双重撤销风险，且已完成交易可能在交割后被任何一方逆转。NDRC调查聚焦于两个核心国家安全类别：原在中国受训的模型工程人才离岸转移，以及能够处理大量用户和企业数据的技术资产跨境转移。买方应预期中国国家安全审查将成为跨境科技交易的常规交割条件，尽职调查清单需新增中国国家安全维度。
